1	# Getting started (local dev)
2	
3	## Prerequisites
4	
5	- **conda** (the backend uses a conda env — not venv/poetry), **Docker** + Docker
6	  Compose, and **Node 24+ / pnpm 9+** for the frontend.
7	
8	## One-command setup
9	
10	```bash
11	git clone https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ.git
12	cd DataQ
13	./scripts/setup.sh     # creates the `dataq` conda env, installs pre-commit, pulls
14	                       # images, runs DB migrations, seeds dev data, writes a local .env
15	conda activate dataq
16	docker-compose up      # Postgres + Redis + FastAPI (:8000) + React (:3000) + Celery
17	```
18	
19	Local auth uses a **dev-bypass** (no Azure tenant needed) — every request resolves to a
20	fixed dev user. Real Azure AD SSO is configured via environment variables in deployed
21	environments.
22	
23	## Configuration
24	
25	All runtime config is environment variables read by the backend's `Settings`. The
26	**complete, commented reference** is
27	[`.env.app.example`](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/blob/main/.env.app.example) —
28	copy it to `.env.app` (gitignored) and adjust. Never commit secrets; `scripts/setup.sh`
29	generates local-dev credentials on first run.
30	
31	## Running tests
32	
33	```bash
34	# Backend (needs a Postgres; CI provides one — locally set TEST_DATABASE_URL):
35	conda run -n dataq python -m pytest backend/tests
36	
37	# Frontend:
38	cd frontend && pnpm test
39	```
40	
41	Before pushing, run the same gate CI does: Ruff, Black `--check`, mypy, Bandit, pytest
42	(backend) and ESLint, Prettier `--check`, Vitest (frontend). See the
43	**[Contributing guide](contributing.md)**.
44	
```

Real Azure AD SSO is configured via environment variables in deployed\nenvironments.",
  "new_string": "# Getting started\n\nTwo tracks, matched to why you're here:\n\n- **Run / evaluate / self-host** → pull the prebuilt images (below). Recommended.\n- **Develop / contribute** → build from source with `scripts/setup.sh` ([further down](#develop-from-source)).\n\n## Run from prebuilt images (recommended)\n\n**Prerequisite:** Docker (Compose v2). No source checkout, no conda, no Node, no Azure\ntenant.\n\n```bash\ncurl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/main/docker-compose.ghcr.yml\ndocker compose -f docker-compose.ghcr.yml up\n```\n\nThis pulls the published images from GHCR and brings up Postgres + Redis + the API +\nCelery worker + the UI, runs migrations, and seeds demo data. Open\n**`http://localhost:3000`** — you're in, on **dev-bypass auth** (every request resolves\nto a fixed demo user; no sign-in). API + Swagger at `http://localhost:8000/docs`.\n\n- **Multi-arch:** the images are `linux/amd64` + `linux/arm64`, so Apple Silicon runs\n  native (not emulated).\n- **Loopback-only:** every port binds to `127.0.0.1` — the stack is reachable from your\n  own machine but never the LAN (it deliberately disables auth and runs a passwordless\n  DB, so it must not be network-exposed). **Not for production** — a real deploy uses the\n  Terraform stack (`deploy/terraform`, ADR 0024).\n- **Pin a release** instead of the moving stable tags:\n  `DATAQ_BACKEND_TAG=vX.Y.Z DATAQ_FRONTEND_TAG=vX.Y.Z docker compose -f docker-compose.ghcr.yml up`.\n- **Reset:** `docker compose -f docker-compose.ghcr.yml down -v` (drops the seeded DB).\n\n### Self-hosting with your own Azure AD\n\nThe `:dev` frontend image the compose pulls is the **zero-config eval build** — auth is\nbypassed, so it's for evaluation, not a real multi-user deployment. Because Vite bakes\nauth config into the bundle at build time, a prebuilt image can't carry *your* tenant:\n\n- The published **`:latest`** frontend is a production base with **no tenant baked in**\n  (it shows an \"authentication not configured\" banner as-pulled). For real SSO, build the\n  frontend from source with your `VITE_AZURE_TENANT_ID` / `VITE_AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID` /\n  `VITE_AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID` (see [`frontend/Dockerfile`](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/blob/main/frontend/Dockerfile)),\n  and run the **backend** with `AUTH_DEV_BYPASS` off + the matching `AZURE_*` settings.\n- The prebuilt UI images reverse-proxy `/api` + `/mcp` to the backend over **Docker's\n  embedded DNS** (`127.0.0.1:53`), so they target the Compose network; outside Compose\n  (e.g. Kubernetes) front them with your own ingress instead.\n- **MCP** (`/mcp`) is Azure-AD-protected and **fail-closed**, so it does not function in\n  the dev-bypass eval stack — it needs real auth configured.\n\n## Develop from source\n\n**Prerequisites:** **conda** (the backend uses a conda env — not venv/poetry),\n**Docker** + Docker Compose, and **Node 24+ / pnpm 9+** for the frontend.\n\n```bash\ngit clone https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ.git\ncd DataQ\n./scripts/setup.sh     # creates the `dataq` conda env, installs pre-commit, pulls\n                       # images, runs DB migrations, seeds dev data, writes a local .env\nconda activate dataq\ndocker-compose up      # Postgres + Redis + FastAPI (:8000) + React (:3000) + Celery\n```\n\nLocal auth uses a **dev-bypass** (no Azure tenant needed) — every request resolves to a\nfixed dev user. Real Azure AD SSO is configured via environment variables in deployed\nenvironments."
}

1	# DataQ — deployment guide
2	
3	How DataQ v1 is deployed to Azure. Infrastructure is **in-repo Terraform**
4	(`deploy/terraform/`, applied — [ADR 0024](../docs/adr/0024-app-deployment-infrastructure.md));
5	the app rolls out via the **`Deploy`** workflow
6	([.github/workflows/deploy.yml](../.github/workflows/deploy.yml), `workflow_dispatch`).
7	The stack is **live** — this is the runbook to provision a fresh environment and to
8	deploy a new image. Related: [ADR 0025](../docs/adr/0025-production-image-pip-slim.md)
9	(slim+pip image), [ADR 0023](../docs/adr/0023-container-image-registry-ghcr.md) (GHCR).
10	
11	Azure is **one** deploy target behind the app's seams (ADR 0010/0013) — the
12	manifests here are infra config, not business logic. No Azure resource names are
13	hardcoded in app code; they live only as Terraform vars + workflow `vars`/`secrets`.
14	
15	## Topology
16	
17	```
18	Browser ─► Azure Static Web App (frontend/dist)
19	              │  /api/* proxied to the linked backend (same-origin → no CORS)
20	              ▼
21	        Azure Container Apps
22	          • dataq-api     (FastAPI image, external ingress :8000)
23	          • dataq-worker  (same image, `celery -A ... worker` + beat)
24	          • dataq-migrate (Container Apps Job: `alembic upgrade head`)
25	              │
26	              ├─► Azure Database for PostgreSQL (DATABASE_URL)
27	              ├─► Azure Cache for Redis        (REDIS_URL)
28	              ├─► Azure Key Vault              (SECRET_STORE=azure_key_vault, managed identity)
29	              └─► Application Insights         (APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING)
30	        GitHub Container Registry (GHCR) — holds the backend image (ADR 0023)
31	          ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-backend:<tag> — public package, so ACA
32	          pulls it anonymously (no registry credential stored on the apps/job).
33	```
34	
35	Both api + worker run the **same** image ([backend/Dockerfile](../backend/Dockerfile),
36	build context = repo root). The frontend is built and uploaded to SWA by the
37	workflow (the [frontend/Dockerfile](../frontend/Dockerfile) is the container
38	alternative — only needed if you run the UI on Container Apps instead of SWA).
39	
40	## One-time provisioning
41	
42	The datasource + compute infra is stood up by the external Terraform harness
43	(ADR 0021) — see `HARNESS_TODO.md`. Beyond that, this app needs:
44	
45	1. An **ACA environment** + the three apps/job above (the backend image is on
46	   **GHCR**, not ACR — ADR 0023). The api/worker run `uvicorn …` / `celery …`;
47	   the migrate **job** runs `alembic upgrade head`. The `deploy/terraform/` stack
48	   provisions all of this; the GHCR package must be **public** so ACA pulls it
49	   anonymously.
50	2. **Managed identity** on the api + worker apps with **Key Vault Secrets User**
51	   on the vault (so `DefaultAzureCredential` resolves `SECRET_STORE=azure_key_vault`).
52	3. **App env**: set the keys on the api + worker apps. The **complete** env-var
53	   reference (every Settings key) is [../.env.app.example](../.env.app.example);
54	   the prod-specific *values* are in [deploy/.env.app.prod.example](.env.app.prod.example).
55	   Secret values (DB/Redis URL, App Insights, webhook URLs) are Key Vault-backed
56	   Container Apps secrets — never literals. The user-assigned managed identity
57	   needs `AZURE_CLIENT_ID` set so `DefaultAzureCredential` resolves it (#408).
58	4. **SWA linked backend**: link the `dataq-api` Container App as the SWA backend so
59	   `/api/*` is proxied same-origin (then `CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS` can stay empty). If
60	   instead the SPA calls the API cross-origin, set `CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS` to the SWA
61	   origin (the FastAPI CORS middleware turns on only when it's non-empty).
62	5. **Azure Monitor → ADF webhook** alert rule (Week-7 task) — needs the deployed
63	   API URL; configure after the first deploy. Per [ADR 0006](../docs/adr/0006-adf-webhook-authentication.md)
64	   the shared secret rides the URL as a `?token=` query param, so don't
65	   hand-assemble it (wrong host / stale token after rotation / missing `?token=`
66	   are easy to get wrong — #92).
67	
68	   **Easiest path: the in-app webhook-config surface (#490).** Sign in as a
69	   workspace admin → **Settings → Webhooks** to copy the ready-to-paste ADF
70	   URL (host + current `?token=` from Key Vault) and the Airflow URL. Set
71	   `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` so the generated host is the public origin (the deploy sets
72	   it to the SWA host; empty falls back to the request host). Paste the ADF URL
73	   into the Action Group webhook field. Note the **live ADF delivery still needs
74	   the Common-Alert-Schema payload mapping (#492)** — the alert body Azure Monitor
75	   sends differs from what the receiver parses today.
76	
77	   Or build it from the CLI (the live host + Key Vault secret):
78	
79	   ```bash
80	   # Vars you already set for the deploy workflow + the vault name.
81	   RG=<AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP>; API_APP_NAME=<API_APP_NAME>; VAULT=<key-vault-name>
82	   API_HOST=$(az containerapp show -n "$API_APP_NAME" -g "$RG" \
83	     --query properties.configuration.ingress.fqdn -o tsv)
84	   # ADF_WEBHOOK_SECRET_NAME (default 'adf-webhook-secret') is the Key Vault *key*.
85	   TOKEN=$(az keyvault secret show --vault-name "$VAULT" --name adf-webhook-secret \
86	     --query value -o tsv)
87	   printf 'ADF webhook URL: https://%s/api/v1/orchestration/events/adf?token=%s\n' \
88	     "$API_HOST" "$TOKEN"
89	   ```
90	
91	   ⚠️ The printed URL **contains the shared secret**. Paste it straight into the
92	   Action Group webhook config; never commit it, and don't run this where the
93	   output is captured to a log (CI, `script`, screen-share). The secret has a
94	   single source of truth (Key Vault), so re-run after a rotation
95	   ([ADR 0006](../docs/adr/0006-adf-webhook-authentication.md) is a hard cutover).
96	
97	   The token is placed in the URL **un-encoded**, and the receiver compares the
98	   *URL-decoded* `token` against the Key Vault value — so the webhook secret must
99	   be **URL-safe** (generate it as e.g. `openssl rand -hex 32`). If an existing
100	   secret contains reserved characters (`+` `/` `=` `&` `#` space), percent-encode
101	   the token in the pasted URL, or it will silently fail auth (401).
102	
103	   The **Airflow** callback URL is the sibling endpoint but carries **no secret**
104	   — it's HMAC-signed in a header ([ADR 0007](../docs/adr/0007-airflow-callback-model.md)),
105	   with the signing key configured in the DAG snippet ([integrations/airflow/](../integrations/airflow/)),
106	   not the URL — so it's just `https://$API_HOST/api/v1/orchestration/events/airflow`.
107	
108	## GitHub config the workflow reads
109	
110	Set under repo **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions**, and add a
111	federated credential for OIDC login (subject = this repo's `production`
112	environment).
113	
114	**Secrets:** `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`, `AZURE_TENANT_ID`, `AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID`
115	(OIDC app registration), `AZURE_STATIC_WEB_APPS_API_TOKEN`. The GHCR image push
116	uses the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` (`packages: write`) — no registry secret to set.
117	
118	**Variables:** `AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP`, `API_APP_NAME`, `WORKER_APP_NAME`,
119	`MIGRATE_JOB_NAME`, and the non-secret `VITE_AZURE_*` build values. (No `ACR_*` —
120	the image lives on GHCR at a fixed `ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-backend` path.)
121	
122	## Going live
123	
124	1. Provision the resources + set the secrets/vars above.
125	2. Run the **Deploy** workflow manually (`workflow_dispatch`) to validate end-to-end.
126	3. To deploy on every merge, uncomment the `push: branches: [main]` trigger in
127	   the workflow.
128	
129	Migrations are additive/backward-compatible (CLAUDE.md), so the workflow runs
130	`alembic upgrade head` **before** rolling the apps — the running old code
131	tolerates the new schema. (This is exactly the dev-DB step that, when skipped,
132	500s the checks endpoint after a schema-adding deploy.)
133	
134	Use an **immutable** `image_tag` per release — ACA caches a tag at the node, so a
135	same-tag rebuild won't be re-pulled on a new revision. Push-on-merge is
136	intentionally **off**; deploys are manual `workflow_dispatch`.
137	
138	## Verify
139	
140	- `GET /healthz` → `200 {"status":"ok"}`.
141	- `GET /api/v1/me` → **401** (auth enforced; a valid token resolves the user).
142	- SPA root + a deep link → 200; sign-in via Azure AD SSO.
143	- Interactive API docs (`/docs`, `/redoc`, `/openapi.json`) are **404 in prod**
144	  (#170 — the prod-docs gate); the MCP server is mounted at `/mcp` (Azure-AD
145	  validated; fail-closed without auth — [ADR 0008](../docs/adr/0008-mcp-server.md)).
146	- Celery beat starts clean (no `NoneType` lock crash, #405/#407) and orchestration
147	  polling reads Key Vault secrets (#406/#408).
148	
149	## Operational notes
150	
151	- **Restart dependent Container Apps after a shared-Postgres delete/recreate** —
152	  the DB host is injected as a start-time secret snapshot, so every dependent
153	  revision must be restarted or it keeps resolving the old/dead host.
154	- The shared RG / Container Apps env / Postgres server are **reused, never
155	  destroyed** (free/trial caps one of each; shared with the harness — ADR 0024).
156	- `key_vault_purge_protection` is off during bring-up (so a destroy/re-apply can
157	  reuse the vault name); set it **true** for a hardened prod (irreversible).
158	- **Workspace-admins are superusers over every suite** ([ADR 0027](../docs/adr/0027-suite-permission-model-workspace-admin.md) / #482):
159	  anyone in `WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS` can read **all** suites' results — including
160	  failing-row samples (`results.sample_failures`), the one place PII/PHI lands —
161	  and manage/delete any suite. **Keep the allowlist minimal.** For a **PHI / regulated
162	  deployment**, treat the data-access audit trail (G1 / #431 in
163	  [compliance-posture.md](../docs/compliance-posture.md)) as a **prerequisite before
164	  granting broad workspace-admin** — PHI is already G1-blocked, and this access breadth
165	  raises the bar.
166	
```

> DEVELOPER

Hey. Are we overcomplicating the things, or this is how it is for BYOL projects?

> AGENT

Honest answer: **~80% of it is just what BYOL work is, and ~20% is one genuine complexity smell we inherited** — not something this task invented.

**The standard, unavoidable parts** (every self-hosted/BYOL project does these):
- Multi-arch images — table stakes once you distribute images.
- A pull-based compose that migrates + seeds — *the* canonical "try it in 5 min" pattern.
- A same-origin reverse proxy so the SPA and API share an origin without a cloud load balancer — standard for shipping an SPA+API together.
- Splitting "run from image" vs "build from source" docs — normal.

None of that is over-engineering; it's the price of "someone else runs this on their machine."

**The one real smell — the two frontend images (`:latest` + `:dev`).** That exists *only* because the SPA bakes its auth config into the bundle at build time (Vite inlines `VITE_*`), and dev-bypass is tied to `import.meta.env.DEV`. That single design choice is what forced: two images, the awkward "`:latest` shows an unconfigured banner as-pulled," and the `NODE_ENV=development` trick. That's not inherent to BYOL — it's a build-time-config decision leaking into distribution.

**How mature self-hosted SPAs avoid it:** make auth config *runtime*, not build-time. The container serves a tiny `/config.json` (or `window.__ENV`) that nginx fills from env at startup, and the SPA reads it at boot. Then **one** image works for both the eval demo *and* a real self-hoster's Azure AD — they just pass their tenant as env vars at `docker run`, no rebuild. And here's the kicker: **we already built the mechanism** — the nginx `envsubst`-at-startup we added for `DATAQ_API_UPSTREAM` is exactly what would inject that config. So collapsing two images into one is a small, natural follow-up, not a rewrite.

**Verdict:** for a single-tenant, Azure-first v1 that's 8 weeks in, what we shipped is proportionate and well-documented — I wouldn't unwind it now. But if BYOL becomes a real distribution channel post-v1, the **runtime-frontend-config** change is the one simplification worth making: it deletes the second image, the "unusable `:latest`" sharp edge, and the docs caveats that go with them.

Also worth separating: the *process* volume (3 PRs, reviews, CI waits) isn't overcomplication — that's this repo's own working agreements (one-functionality commits, review-before-merge). That's discipline you've chosen, not overhead I added.

Want me to file that runtime-config idea as a post-v1 issue so it's captured against `context/post-v1-roadmap.md`?

> DEVELOPER

How much effort is that to make the change now?

> AGENT

Good news: the code is shaped so this is a **half-day change, one PR** — not a refactor. The reason it's cheap is that `authConfig`/`authMode` are computed **synchronously at module load** and `index.html` loads the app as a deferred module script. So I can inject a **synchronous global before the bundle runs** and nothing downstream changes.

**The approach** (reuses the envsubst we already built — no new moving parts):
- `index.html` gets a blocking `<script src="/config.js">` in `<head>` (runs before the deferred module bundle).
- nginx serves `/config.js` from a `location = /config.js { return 200 'window.__DATAQ_CONFIG__={...}' }` in the **already-envsubst'd** `nginx.conf.template`, filled from `${DATAQ_AZURE_*}` env at container start.
- `config.ts` reads `window.__DATAQ_CONFIG__` first, falls back to `import.meta.env` for `pnpm dev`. Its six consumers don't change at all.

**Effort, file by file (~4–5 hrs):**

| Work | Effort |
|---|---|
| `config.ts` read window-global + `window.d.ts` type | ~30 min |
| `index.html` config script + dev fallback | ~20 min |
| `nginx.conf.template` `/config.js` location + Dockerfile ENV defaults | ~30 min |
| **Delete** the two-image machinery: Dockerfile `VITE_*`/`BUILD_NODE_ENV` args, the `:dev` variant in `publish-images.yml`, compose → single `:latest` + env | ~45 min |
| Rewrite `config.test.ts` (62 lines) to drive the runtime global | ~45 min |
| Docs: remove the `:latest`-unconfigured / two-image caveats | ~30 min |
| Local verify (one image, dev-bypass **and** simulated real-auth via env) + review + PR + CI | ~60 min |

**What it buys:** one frontend image instead of two, the `NODE_ENV=development` trick gone, the "`:latest` shows an unconfigured banner" sharp edge gone, real self-host becomes "set env vars at `docker run`" (no rebuild), and the docs shrink.

**The one caveat you should weigh:** this moves dev-bypass from build-time to runtime, which effectively **reverses the decision you made earlier** (you chose "two tags" *over* relaxing the `import.meta.env.DEV` guard). It's cleaner here — bypass is an explicit operator env var and the backend still enforces auth regardless — but it does remove that build-time guardrail, so it's a conscious re-decision, and it'll trip the same security-review flag we hit on the compose (mitigated the same way: the image is safe, the operator opts into bypass).

My take: it's genuinely worth doing and cheap, but it's **not urgent for an Azure-first v1** — the current thing works and is documented. If you're planning to lean on BYOL post-v1, I'd do it then (or now if you want the distribution story clean before v1 ships). Want me to do it now, or file it against `context/post-v1-roadmap.md`?

That constraint actually fits this change well — and it sharpens what belongs *in* it versus what's a separate, larger piece. Let me be precise about the boundary, because "cloud-neutral" has two layers here:

**Layer 1 — the image + config mechanism (this change delivers it, cleanly):**
The whole point of runtime config injection is that **the image carries zero cloud specifics** — everything comes from env at `docker run`. So one generic image runs on Azure, AWS, GCP, or a laptop; only the injected values differ. To make it *properly* neutral rather than "Azure values injected," I'd shape the config as a **generic identity contract**, not Azure fields:

```js

  auth: {
    mode: "bypass" | "oidc",        // "bypass" = local/eval, no IdP
    provider: "azure_ad",           // impl selector (only one wired in v1)
    authority: "https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/v2.0",
    clientId: "…",
    apiScope: "…",

}
```

Env vars become `DATAQ_AUTH_MODE` / `DATAQ_AUTH_AUTHORITY` / `DATAQ_AUTH_CLIENT_ID` / `DATAQ_AUTH_API_SCOPE` / `DATAQ_AUTH_PROVIDER` — **no `AZURE` in the image or the contract**. Azure is just one populated shape; the fields map cleanly onto MSAL (`authority`, `clientId`, `scope`) so nothing is contorted. This is consistent with your existing anti-lock-in seams (ADR 0010/0013 — a generic seam, Azure as the one impl). Cost: **+1–2 hrs** on top of the half-day.

**Layer 2 — actually authenticating against AWS/GCP IdPs (NOT this change):**
The frontend's auth *library* is **MSAL**, which is Azure-AD-specific. A generic config contract lets you *express* a Cognito/Identity-Platform/Keycloak authority, but MSAL won't talk to them. Real non-Azure sign-in needs a **generic OIDC client** (e.g. `oidc-client-ts`) behind an auth-provider seam — that's the larger, separate effort that lines up with the AWS/GCP "planned" status. I'd **not** build it now; the config contract just leaves the door open so no future image change is needed.

- **Backend** is already neutral at the boundary (`get_current_user`, no Entra-claim reads — CLAUDE.md §11), so it's ready.
- **Local** is trivially neutral: `mode: "bypass"` needs no IdP at all.

So the honest scope: **this change makes the package and config genuinely cloud-neutral (one image, generic contract, ~half a day + ~1–2 hrs)** and delivers Azure + local out of the box. It does **not** make non-Azure IdPs work — that's the deferred OIDC-client seam, and I'd file it as the post-v1 companion.

Want me to **do the cloud-neutral runtime-config change now** (one image, generic `DATAQ_AUTH_*` contract, Azure+bypass working) and **file the generic-OIDC-client seam** against `context/post-v1-roadmap.md`? Or file both and hold?

> DEVELOPER

Also, we need to make the deep bypass off by default. It has to be explicitly flip in order to be enabled.

> AGENT

That's the right call, and it actually makes the whole thing *more* secure than what we have today. Here's how it lands:

**Bypass becomes fail-closed by construction.** In the runtime-config model the image bakes *nothing* — so there's no bypass baked into any published artifact. Auth mode resolves like this, with bypass never a fallback:

```
mode = window.__DATAQ_CONFIG__.auth.mode          // injected at runtime
- unset / anything but "bypass"  → real auth (oidc) if authority+clientId present, else "unconfigured" banner
- exactly "bypass"               → dev-bypass  (the ONLY way in)
```

So a plain `docker run` with no env → **not** bypassed (shows "unconfigured", backend returns 401). Bypass turns on **only** when the operator explicitly sets `DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=bypass` — and our eval compose is the one place that does the explicit flip (alongside the backend's `AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true`, which already defaults to `False`). Both layers off-by-default, both explicitly opted in only for the eval stack.

**Why this is a net security win:** today's published `:dev` image is literally an auth-disabled build sitting on a public registry — pull it, deploy it, you've got no auth. The runtime model **deletes that artifact entirely**; nothing shippable has bypass baked, so the "off by default, explicit flip" property is structural, not a convention.

**Consolidated plan** (all three of your constraints):
1. **One cloud-neutral image** — config injected at runtime via nginx-envsubst'd `/config.js` (no cloud, no bypass baked).
2. **Generic `DATAQ_AUTH_*` contract** (`mode` / `provider` / `authority` / `clientId` / `apiScope`) — Azure is one populated shape via MSAL; the OIDC client for non-Azure IdPs is the deferred post-v1 seam.
3. **Bypass off by default, explicit `mode=bypass` to enable** — never inferred; verified by testing that a config-less image is *not* bypassed.

**Effort:** ~half a day + ~1–2 hrs for the generic schema ≈ **one PR, ~5–6 hrs**. I'll explicitly test the fail-closed property and expect (and pre-mitigate) the security-review flag.

Two things I'd still file rather than build now: the **generic OIDC client** (real AWS/GCP/Keycloak sign-in) and — worth confirming — do you want me to **keep the current `:dev` image working until this lands**, or is it fine that this PR removes it and the eval compose switches to `:latest` + `DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=bypass` in the same change?

Can we check this generic OIDC client with Azure as well?

> AGENT

Yes — and that's actually the smartest way to de-risk it, because it could collapse the whole thing to **one auth client for every provider including Azure**.

**Why it works:** Azure AD is a standards-compliant OIDC provider. Its authority (`https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/v2.0`) exposes the normal discovery doc, and the SPA flow (authorization code + PKCE) is vanilla OIDC. So a generic client like `oidc-client-ts` can authenticate against Azure just as it would against Cognito, GCP Identity Platform, or Keycloak. If it holds up, you get **one auth stack for Azure + AWS + GCP + local**, no MSAL, and the config contract simplifies to just `mode: bypass | oidc` + `authority`/`clientId`/`apiScope` — you don't even need a `provider` discriminator.

**The catch — it means replacing MSAL, which is the path that's live in production right now.** So this isn't free:
- The token work we just shipped (#168 `InteractionRequiredAuthError` fallback) and the silent-refresh in the interceptor are MSAL-specific; they'd be redone in `oidc-client-ts` terms (it has its own silent-renew + renew-error → redirect handling).
- You trade MSAL's Azure-tuned conveniences for standard OIDC.

**What the spike must actually prove (this is the whole risk):** the login redirect is vanilla OIDC and will "just work" — the Azure-specific behavior lives in **acquiring an access token for your API scope** (`api://<api-client-id>/user_impersonation`) and **silent renew**. That's the exact thing to verify against the real tenant. If the generic client cleanly gets that API-scoped token and renews it silently → **retire MSAL, one client for all**. If Azure throws a quirk that needs MSAL → fall back to the seam (MSAL for Azure + OIDC for others, two impls).

**So the recommendation for the deferred issue:** frame it as *"generic OIDC client, validated against Azure first — if the API-scope token + silent renew are clean, drop MSAL entirely."* That's the outcome you want (one stack), and checking Azure up front is what decides it.

None of this changes the immediate move — the runtime-config / one-image / bypass-off-by-default change stands on its own, and the generic `DATAQ_AUTH_*` contract we're adding makes *either* auth outcome a drop-in later (no image change needed).

So, to lock scope: I'll **do the runtime-config change now** (cloud-neutral image, generic contract, bypass fail-closed), and **file the OIDC issue as "validate against Azure first → retire MSAL if clean, else two-impl seam."** Green light?

# Final verdict

**All three are the right goal — but they sit at three different maturity stages, and only two are "now." The discipline that keeps this from becoming over-engineering is: build the *seams* now, defer the second *implementations* until there's a real second target.**

### 1. Multi-architecture — ✅ Done, non-negotiable
`amd64` + `arm64` is already shipped and verified on GHCR. Cheap, standard, zero downside. Nothing more to do.

### 2. Generic container image — ✅ Do it now
One image per component, **nothing baked in** — no cloud, no secrets, no auth-bypass. Config injected at runtime (`/config.js` via the nginx envsubst we already have). This is ~½ day and is a **strict improvement** even for an Azure-only v1:
- Deletes the two-image split, the `NODE_ENV` trick, and the "`:latest` shows unconfigured" edge.
- **Removes the auth-disabled `:dev` artifact from a public registry** — bypass becomes structurally fail-closed (off by default, explicit `mode=bypass` only).
- Real self-host becomes "set env vars," not "rebuild."

There is no good reason to keep cloud/bypass baked into an image. Do this.

### 3. Multi-vendor — 🟡 Seam now, implementation later
Split it honestly into two layers:

- **The neutral surface (now, ~free):** the generic image + a provider-shaped `DATAQ_AUTH_*` config contract, on top of the backend boundaries you already have (`get_current_user`, `SecretStore`, `ResultPublisher`, `OrchestrationProvider`). After this, **the image and contract are genuinely cloud-neutral** — Azure is just the one populated shape, and moving to another vendor needs **no image change**.
- **Actual AWS/GCP (post-v1, real work):** a **generic OIDC client validated against Azure first** (if the API-scope token + silent renew are clean, retire MSAL → one auth stack for all; else MSAL-for-Azure + OIDC-for-others), **plus** AWS/GCP Terraform. Neither exists today; both are tracked, not built.

### The guardrail (this is the anti-overcomplication rule)
**Do not build the OIDC client or AWS/GCP IaC now.** For an Azure-first v1, that's speculative — a seam with one impl is correct; a *second impl* with no second target is the over-engineering you asked about at the start. The generic contract keeps the door open at ~zero cost; walking through it waits for a real customer/target.

### Bottom line
> **One multi-arch image per component, nothing baked in, config + auth + secrets injected at runtime behind generic seams, bypass fail-closed, Azure as the single wired implementation.** That end-state is fully cloud-neutral *in packaging and contract* today, and makes genuine AWS/GCP support a drop-in later — without paying for a second implementation before you need it.

Concretely: **do the runtime-config / one-image / bypass-off-by-default change now** (cloud-neutral, ~½ day + ~1–2 hrs for the generic contract), and **file two post-v1 issues** — the Azure-validated generic OIDC client, and AWS/GCP deploy IaC. That's the proportionate path.

# Architecture Decision Records (ADRs)

Each ADR captures a single significant architecture decision: the context, the decision, the consequences, and the alternatives considered. New ADRs are append-only — supersede an old decision by adding a new ADR and marking the old one's status as `Superseded by ADR-NNNN`.

## Format

- File name: `NNNN-short-kebab-slug.md` (zero-padded 4-digit sequence)
- Frontmatter fields:
  - **Status** — one of `Proposed`, `Accepted`, `Deprecated`, `Superseded by ADR-NNNN` (title-case)
  - **Date** — `YYYY-MM-DD`
  - **Deciders** — who made the call
  - **Consulted** *(optional)* — stakeholders whose sign-off the decision needed (e.g. product owner for ADR 0005). Omit when none.
  - **Supersedes** *(optional)* — `ADR-NNNN` this decision replaces. Omit when none.
  - **Superseded by** *(optional)* — `ADR-NNNN` that later replaced this one. Add when the status flips to `Superseded by`.
- Sections: Context, Decision, Consequences, Alternatives considered, Related (optional)
- Keep each ADR short — 1–2 pages. If it grows past that, the decision is probably two decisions.

### Template

```markdown
...
| [0019](0019-custom-sql-check-kind.md) | Custom-SQL checks ride `kind='expectation'` via GX `UnexpectedRowsExpectation` (no new kind); read-only validation + SQL-datasource gating | Accepted |
| [0020](0020-history-and-audit-strategy.md) | History/audit: per-entity Type-4 snapshot tables (`check_versions`, `connection_versions`) where config history is needed; no SCD-2; credentials never snapshotted; cascade-delete accepted; cross-entity audit log deferred | Accepted |
| [0021](0021-demo-test-data-environment-strategy.md) | Live test/demo-data environment (retail model, 3 reference flows) lives outside the repo — Terraform/mock-data/Databricks notebook not git-tracked; discharges the deferred live-warehouse/file smoke | Accepted |
| [0022](0022-week6-prototype-adoption-and-chart-library.md) | Week-6 prototype adoption — full 13-screen set as dedicated pages (Share is the only drawer; prototype wins on conflicts; Settings/Admin pulled into W6); chart library = recharts (lazy-loaded) | Accepted |
| [0023](0023-container-image-registry-ghcr.md) | Container image registry — GitHub Container Registry (GHCR) over ACR / Docker Hub (vendor-neutral, public package → anonymous ACA pull, reuses `GITHUB_TOKEN`); supersedes the #379 ACR scaffolding | Accepted |
| [0024](0024-app-deployment-infrastructure.md) | App deploy infra — in-repo Terraform; shares subscription/RG/ACA-env/Postgres with the harness; ACA api+worker+migrate-job + SWA-Standard linked same-origin `/api` + self-hosted Redis + KV (UAMI) + App Insights + AAD-app-reg OIDC | Accepted |
| [0025](0025-production-image-pip-slim.md) | Production image — multi-stage `python:3.13-slim` + pip (not conda; ~2.84GB→~1GB); conda stays the local-dev tool; amends the W1 conda lock | Accepted |

# ADR 0026 — DataQ-issued API keys / service tokens behind the auth seam (REST + MCP)

- **Status:** Proposed
- **Date:** 2026-06-29
- **Deciders:** @TheurgicDuke771
- **Related:** ADR [0010](0010-provider-agnostic-infrastructure-seams.md) (the `get_current_user` identity seam — Azure is one impl, not the architecture), [0013](0013-marketplace-distribution-and-anti-lock-in.md) (BYOL / anti-lock-in), [0008](0008-mcp-server.md) (MCP auth via `JWTVerifier` — bring-your-own-token today), [0020](0020-history-and-audit-strategy.md) (audit), compliance posture (#436)
- **Issue:** [#461](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/461)

> **Stub — Proposed, not yet designed in full.** Captures the direction while it's fresh; to be fleshed out when Theme 3 (access/identity) is picked up post-v1.

## Context

Authentication today is **exclusively Azure AD bearer tokens** (delegated/SSO) for both the REST API and `/mcp`. There is no DataQ-native credential. Two problems follow:

1. **Lock-in.** This is the deepest remaining Azure coupling. The `get_current_user` seam (ADR 0010) exists and service code never reads Entra claims (CLAUDE.md §11), but the seam has exactly *one* real implementation, and the persistence layer is still Azure-shaped (`users.aad_object_id`). A BYOL customer on AWS/GCP (ADR 0013) has no Azure AD and cannot authenticate at all.
2. **No programmatic access.** Headless agents, CI, and always-on MCP clients want a long-lived, scoped, revocable secret — not a ~60-min Azure token they must refresh (ADR 0008 uses a token-*validating* `JWTVerifier`, not a client-driven OAuth provider). There is no API-key / PAT / service-token mechanism.

## Decision (direction — to be detailed)

Introduce a **DataQ-issued credential as a second authenticator behind the existing `get_current_user` seam**, so the **REST API and `/mcp` accept it identically** — explicitly *not* an MCP-only feature. On MCP, fastmcp `MultiAuth` lets `/mcp` accept either a DataQ key or an Azure token. Adding a second real auth impl is also what *exercises* (and thereby validates) the seam ADR 0010 describes.

**Phased:**

1. **User-scoped PATs first.** A key belongs to a user and inherits that user's per-suite grants → **no new authz model** (reuse the `view < edit < admin < owner` ladder; optionally down-scope a key to read-only — ideal for MCP read tools / dashboards, smallest blast radius). ~80% of the value for a fraction of the change.
2. **Service-account principals later.** These force the larger move and should be sequenced after PATs prove the seam: generalize `users.aad_object_id` into a generic **principal** with pluggable identity bindings (Azure AD oid, API key, …), and extend suite **sharing** to non-user principals.

**Credential bar (this is a new secret surface — not to be half-built):**

- Hash-at-rest (argon2/bcrypt), **show-once** on creation, identifying prefix (`dq_live_…`), expiry defaults, revocation, last-used + audit.
- Hashes live in a **new `api_keys` table** — *not* the credential SecretStore (that store is for *retrievable* connection secrets; a key hash is a verifier secret, never retrievable).
- **Lifecycle tied to the owner**: deactivating a user kills their keys, so a PAT can't become an SSO-policy backdoor that outlives the account.
- Never logged (prefix only) — same discipline as the compliance posture (#436).

## Consequences (anticipated)

- Discharges the identity-seam lock-in (ADR 0010/0013): Azure AD becomes *one* authenticator behind the seam, not the only one — unblocking BYOL on non-Azure clouds.
- Closes the programmatic-access gap for REST automation and headless MCP clients without weakening the per-user authz model (PAT phase).
- Adds a credential-management surface (issue/list/revoke UI + API) and an audit obligation.

## Open questions (for the full ADR)
```

The published `:latest` is unusable as-pulled (no tenant baked), and `:dev` is **an auth-disabled artifact sitting on a public registry**.\n2. **Azure lock-in in the SPA** — the frontend authenticates with **MSAL** (`@azure/msal-browser`), an Azure-AD-specific client. The **image + config are not cloud-neutral** — env var names + baked config are Azure-shaped.\n\nGoal: **one multi-arch generic image per component, nothing baked in (no cloud, no secrets, no bypass), config injected at runtime behind generic seams**, with auth-bypass **fail-closed**.\n\n## Scope (v1)\n\n1. **Runtime frontend config injection.** Serve `/config.js` (`window.__DATAQ_CONFIG__`) from the nginx image via the existing envsubst-at-startup; `src/auth/config.ts` reads the runtime global (falls back to `import.meta.env` for `pnpm dev`). Its six consumers don't change. Delete the `VITE_*`/`BUILD_NODE_ENV` build-args + the `:dev` variant → **one frontend image**.\n2. **Generic `DATAQ_AUTH_*` contract** (`mode` / `authority` / `clientId` / `apiScope`; optional `provider`). No `AZURE` in the image or contract — Azure is one populated shape. Provider-agnostic seams (ADR 0010/0013).\n3. **Bypass fail-closed.** `mode` defaults to real/unconfigured; dev-bypass activates **only** on explicit `DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=bypass` (+ backend `AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true`, already default-`false`). If clean → **retire MSAL** (one client for all IdPs incl. local/OIDC/Cognito/Identity-Platform). If Azure needs quirks → fall back to a two-impl seam (MSAL-for-Azure + OIDC-for-others). Rework the #168 `InteractionRequiredAuthError` fallback in OIDC-client terms.\n5. **Deployed-app cutover.** The runtime-config model serves `/config.js` from the nginx **container**, but prod currently serves the UI from **Azure Static Web App** (static, no runtime injection). The generic contract + OIDC client make them a drop-in (no image change).\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- **One** frontend image (multi-arch), zero cloud/secret/bypass baked; the old `:dev` image is gone.\n- `docker run` with no auth env → **not** bypassed (unconfigured banner + backend 401). `DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=bypass` is the only way to enable bypass.\n- Generic OIDC client authenticates against the **live Azure tenant** end-to-end (sign-in + API-scoped token + silent renew + interaction-required fallback). MSAL retired (or a documented Azure-quirk seam if not).\n- Eval compose (`docker-compose.ghcr.yml`) works via `DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=bypass`.\n- Deployed Azure app rebuilt from the images (frontend as a container), KV/App-Insights/Postgres/Redis preserved; real SSO works.\n- ADR 0028 + docs updated.\n\nDesign: ADR 0028 (this change).\nEOF\n)\" 2>&1 | tail -1)\necho \"MAIN ISSUE: $MAIN\"\nPOST=$(gh issue create --title \"Post-v1: AWS + GCP deploy IaC (behind the provider-agnostic seams)\" \\\n  --milestone \"Backlog (post-v1 / testing)\" \\\n  --label \"enhancement\" \\\n  --body \"$(cat <<'EOF'\n## Why\n\nPost-v1 companion to the cloud-neutral image + generic OIDC work. With the generic image + `DATAQ_AUTH_*` contract + generic OIDC client in place, standing up DataQ on AWS or GCP needs **no image change** — only the deploy IaC + the managed-service wiring behind the existing seams.\n\n## Scope (post-v1)\n\n- **AWS:** ECS Fargate / App Runner (api + worker) · RDS for PostgreSQL · ElastiCache for Redis · Secrets Manager (`SecretStore` impl) · CloudWatch + OpenTelemetry · Cognito / OIDC IdP behind `get_current_user`.\n- **GCP:** Cloud Run (api + worker) · Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL · Memorystore for Redis · Secret Manager (`SecretStore` impl) · Cloud Logging + OpenTelemetry · Identity Platform / OIDC IdP.\n\nProvider-agnostic seams: ADR 0010 / 0013. Azure stays the reference impl (ADR 0024).\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- The generic image, runtime config, and OIDC client — those ship in v1 (the cloud-neutral-image issue).\nEOF\n)\" 2>&1 | tail -1)\necho \"POST-V1 ISSUE: $POST\"",

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/docs/adr/0028-cloud-neutral-image-runtime-config-generic-oidc.md",
  "content": "# ADR 0028 — Cloud-neutral image: runtime config injection + generic OIDC auth, bypass fail-closed\n\n- **Status:** Accepted\n- **Date:** 2026-06-30\n- **Deciders:** @TheurgicDuke771\n- **Amends:** ADR [0024](0024-app-deployment-infrastructure.md) (frontend hosting moves Static Web App → a Container App running the nginx image)\n- **Related:** ADR [0010](0010-provider-agnostic-infrastructure-seams.md) (provider-agnostic seams — Azure is one impl), [0013](0013-marketplace-distribution-and-anti-lock-in.md) (BYOL / anti-lock-in), [0023](0023-container-image-registry-ghcr.md) (GHCR), [0025](0025-production-image-pip-slim.md) (slim image), [0008](0008-mcp-server.md) (MCP token validation), [0026](0026-auth-api-keys-and-principal-seam.md) (DataQ-issued credentials — the backend identity seam)\n- **Issue:** [#504](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/504); post-v1 AWS/GCP IaC → [#505](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/505). Follows the prebuilt-image work in [#472](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/472).\n\n## Context\n\nThe prebuilt-image distribution (#472) shipped, but exposed three coupling/complexity\nsmells:\n\n1. **Two frontend images.** Vite inlines `VITE_*` at **build** time, so auth config is\n   baked into the bundle. That forced a `:latest` (production, no tenant baked — shows an\n   \"unconfigured\" banner as-pulled) **and** a `:dev` (dev-bypass) image. The `:dev` image\n   is **an auth-disabled artifact on a public registry** — pull it, deploy it, no auth.\n2. **Azure lock-in in the SPA.** The frontend authenticates with **MSAL**\n   (`@azure/msal-browser`), an Azure-AD-specific client. The backend is already\n   provider-neutral at the boundary (`get_current_user`, no Entra-claim reads —\n   CLAUDE.md §11); the SPA is the remaining coupling.\n3. **The image + config are Azure-shaped** (`VITE_AZURE_*`, baked values), not\n   cloud-neutral.\n\nThe distribution goal (ADR 0013): **one multi-arch generic image per component, nothing\nbaked in — no cloud, no secrets, no auth-bypass — with config injected at runtime behind\ngeneric seams.**\n\n## Decision\n\n1. **Runtime frontend config injection.** The nginx frontend image serves `/config.js`\n   (`window.__DATAQ_CONFIG__ = { auth: { … } }`) rendered from env at container start via\n   the **existing** envsubst-on-templates step (added for `DATAQ_API_UPSTREAM` in #472 — no\n   new moving part). A blocking classic `<script src=\"/config.js\">` in `index.html` runs\n   before the deferred module bundle, so `src/auth/config.ts` reads a **synchronous**\n   global (falling back to `import.meta.env` for `pnpm dev`). Its consumers are unchanged.\n   The `VITE_*` / `BUILD_NODE_ENV` build-args and the `:dev` variant are **deleted → one\n   frontend image**.\n\n2. **Generic `DATAQ_AUTH_*` contract.** The injected config is a provider-shaped identity\n   contract — `mode` (`bypass` | `oidc`), `authority`, `clientId`, `apiScope` (+ optional\n   `provider` for an impl quirk). **No `AZURE` in the image or the contract**; Azure is one\n   populated shape (`authority = https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/v2.0`). This is\n   a seam with one wired impl (ADR 0010) — the *contract* is neutral; a second *impl*\n   waits for a real target.\n\n3. **Bypass fail-closed.** Auth resolves to real/`unconfigured` by default; dev-bypass\n   activates **only** on explicit `DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=bypass` (frontend) + `AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true`\n   (backend, already default `false`). A config-less image is **not** bypassed. The eval\n   compose (`docker-compose.ghcr.yml`) is the single explicit opt-in. Because nothing\n   shippable bakes bypass, \"off by default\" is **structural**, not a convention — a strict\n   security improvement over the retired `:dev` image.\n\n4. **Generic OIDC client, validated against Azure (in v1).** Replace MSAL with a standards\n   OIDC client (e.g. `oidc-client-ts`) and **validate against the live Azure AD tenant**.\n   The login redirect is vanilla OIDC; the risk is acquiring the **API-scope access token**\n   (`api://<api-client-id>/user_impersonation`) + **silent renew**. If clean → **retire\n   MSAL** (one client for Azure, OIDC, Cognito, Identity Platform, Keycloak, local). If\n   Azure needs quirks → fall back to a two-impl seam (MSAL-for-Azure + OIDC-for-others).\n   The #168 `InteractionRequiredAuthError` → interactive fallback is reworked in the OIDC\n   client's silent-renew-error terms.\n\n5. **Deployed-app cutover (amends ADR 0024).** Runtime `/config.js` is served by the nginx\n   **container**, but prod serves the UI from **Static Web App** (static, no runtime\n   injection). So the frontend moves **SWA → a Container App**. Adopt via a **clean\n   rebuild**: remove the DataQ app (api + worker + migrate job + SWA) and rebuild from the\n   new images, **keeping Key Vault, App Insights / Log Analytics, the shared Postgres +\n   `dataq` DB, and Redis as-is**. The deployed app runs `DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=oidc` against the\n   real tenant. AWS/GCP deploy IaC is **post-v1** (#505).\n\n## Consequences\n\n- **One** multi-arch frontend image, cloud-neutral, nothing baked; the auth-disabled `:dev`\n  artifact is gone. Real self-host = set env vars, not rebuild.\n- The last Azure coupling in the SPA is removed (or reduced to a documented seam); combined\n  with ADR 0026 (backend credentials) the platform is genuinely provider-neutral for auth.\n- **Risk:** this replaces MSAL — the auth path currently live in production — so it must be\n  validated end-to-end against the real tenant (API-scoped token + silent renew) before\n  cutover; expect the security review to flag runtime bypass (mitigated: fail-closed +\n  backend enforcement).\n- The deployed frontend changes hosting (SWA → Container App), a one-time cutover with\n  preserved data/secret/observability layers.\n- The generic contract makes AWS/GCP (#505) a drop-in — no future image change.\n\n## Alternatives considered\n\n- **Keep two images (status quo from #472).** Rejected: ships an auth-disabled image on a\n  public registry, `:latest` unusable as-pulled, and the docs carry permanent caveats.\n- **Relax `config.ts` to allow bypass in a production build.** Rejected earlier (the #472\n  two-tag decision) and still: it weakens a guard without solving the cloud-neutrality or\n  MSAL coupling. Runtime config + fail-closed bypass is stronger and more general.\n- **Build-time config (rebuild per environment).** Rejected: defeats \"one generic image\";\n  every self-hoster would rebuild.\n- **MSAL for Azure + OIDC for others (two impls from the start).** Deferred, not chosen up\n  front: validating one generic client against Azure first is what decides whether the\n  second impl is even needed — one stack is simpler if Azure passes.\n- **AWS/GCP IaC now.** Rejected for v1: a second *deploy impl* with no second target is\n  over-engineering; the seam (this ADR) keeps the door open at ~zero cost (#505).\n\n## Related\n\nSupersedes the frontend-hosting half of ADR 0024 (SWA → Container App). Closes the SPA\nside of the anti-lock-in program (ADR 0010/0013); ADR 0026 closes the backend-credential\nside.\n"
}

=== config.ts (current) ===
/**
 * Auth configuration sourced from VITE_* env vars at build time.
 *
 * Mode is computed once at module load:
 * - 'real'         — VITE_AZURE_TENANT_ID + VITE_AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID set.
 *                    MSAL handles redirect-flow login + token acquisition.
 * - 'dev_bypass'   — DEV build + VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true + Azure vars empty.
 *                    No MSAL; renders a fixed dev user. Mirrors backend behaviour.
 * - 'unconfigured' — anything else. AuthGate shows a setup-needed banner.
 */

export type AuthMode = 'real' | 'dev_bypass' | 'unconfigured';

const tenantId = import.meta.env.VITE_AZURE_TENANT_ID;
const spaClientId = import.meta.env.VITE_AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID;
const apiClientId = import.meta.env.VITE_AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID;
const apiScope = import.meta.env.VITE_AZURE_API_SCOPE || 'user_impersonation';
const devBypass = import.meta.env.VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS === 'true';

export const authConfig = {
  tenantId,
  spaClientId,
  apiClientId,
  apiScope,
  apiScopeUri: apiClientId ? `api://${apiClientId}/${apiScope}` : undefined,
} as const;

export const authMode: AuthMode = (() => {
  if (tenantId && spaClientId) return 'real';
  if (import.meta.env.DEV && devBypass) return 'dev_bypass';
  return 'unconfigured';
})();

export const DEV_USER = {
  name: 'Dev Bypass User',
  username: 'dev-bypass@dataq.local',
  homeAccountId: 'dev-bypass',
  isDev: true as const,
};
=== config.test.ts (current) ===
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';

// authMode / authConfig are computed at module load from import.meta.env, so
// each case stubs env then re-imports a fresh module.
beforeEach(() => {
  vi.resetModules();
});

afterEach(() => {
  vi.unstubAllEnvs();
});

async function loadConfig() {
  return import('../../src/auth/config');
}

describe('authMode', () => {
  it("is 'real' when tenant + SPA client id are set", async () => {
    vi.stubEnv('VITE_AZURE_TENANT_ID', 'tenant-1');
    vi.stubEnv('VITE_AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID', 'spa-1');
    const { authMode } = await loadConfig();
    expect(authMode).toBe('real');
  });

  it("is 'dev_bypass' in a DEV build with bypass on and Azure vars empty", async () => {
    vi.stubEnv('VITE_AZURE_TENANT_ID', '');
    vi.stubEnv('VITE_AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID', '');
    vi.stubEnv('VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS', 'true');
    const { authMode } = await loadConfig();
    expect(authMode).toBe('dev_bypass');
  });

  it("is 'unconfigured' when nothing is set and bypass is off", async () => {
    vi.stubEnv('VITE_AZURE_TENANT_ID', '');
    vi.stubEnv('VITE_AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID', '');
    vi.stubEnv('VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS', 'false');
    const { authMode } = await loadConfig();
    expect(authMode).toBe('unconfigured');
  });
});

describe('authConfig.apiScopeUri', () => {
  it('is derived from the API client id and scope', async () => {
    vi.stubEnv('VITE_AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID', 'api-1');
    vi.stubEnv('VITE_AZURE_API_SCOPE', 'access_as_user');
    const { authConfig } = await loadConfig();
    expect(authConfig.apiScopeUri).toBe('api://api-1/access_as_user');
  });

  it('defaults the scope to user_impersonation', async () => {
    vi.stubEnv('VITE_AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID', 'api-1');
    vi.stubEnv('VITE_AZURE_API_SCOPE', '');
    const { authConfig } = await loadConfig();
    expect(authConfig.apiScopeUri).toBe('api://api-1/user_impersonation');
  });

  it('is undefined when no API client id is set', async () => {
    vi.stubEnv('VITE_AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID', '');
    const { authConfig } = await loadConfig();
    expect(authConfig.apiScopeUri).toBeUndefined();
  });
});

=== CurrentUserProvider (how it uses config) ===
import { useMsal } from '@azure/msal-react';
import { useMemo, type ReactNode } from 'react';

import { authMode, DEV_USER } from './config';
import { CurrentUserContext, type CurrentUser } from './currentUserContext';

/**
 * Provides the current user to the tree.
 *
 * - dev_bypass: static dev user.
 * - unconfigured: null (AuthGate shows the banner).
 * - real: subscribes to MSAL accounts via useMsal().
 */
export function CurrentUserProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  if (authMode === 'dev_bypass') {
    return <CurrentUserContext.Provider value={DEV_USER}>{children}</CurrentUserContext.Provider>;
  }
  if (authMode === 'real') {
    return <RealCurrentUserProvider>{children}</RealCurrentUserProvider>;
  }
  return <CurrentUserContext.Provider value={null}>{children}</CurrentUserContext.Provider>;
}

function RealCurrentUserProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  const { accounts } = useMsal();
  const value = useMemo<CurrentUser | null>(() => {
    const account = accounts[0];
    if (!account) return null;
    return {
      name: account.name ?? '(unknown)',
      username: account.username,
      homeAccountId: account.homeAccountId,
      isDev: false,
    };
  }, [accounts]);
  return <CurrentUserContext.Provider value={value}>{children}</CurrentUserContext.Provider>;
}

AuthGate shows a setup-needed banner.\n */\n\nexport type AuthMode = 'real' | 'dev_bypass' | 'unconfigured';\n\n/** The runtime auth contract injected via `window.__DATAQ_CONFIG__.auth`. */\nexport interface DataqAuthConfig {\n  /** 'bypass' = no IdP (local/eval); 'oidc' = real sign-in. Absent → unconfigured. */\n  mode?: 'bypass' | 'oidc';\n  /** OIDC issuer/authority URL (e.g. https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/v2.0). */\n  authority?: string;\n  /** The public SPA client id registered with the IdP. */\n  clientId?: string;\n  /** Full scope string requested for the API access token (Azure: api://<api-client-id>/<scope>). */\n  apiScope?: string;\n}\n\ndeclare global {\n  interface Window {\n    __DATAQ_CONFIG__?: { auth?: DataqAuthConfig };\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Build-time fallback for `pnpm dev` (no injected /config.js). Maps the legacy\n * VITE_* Azure vars onto the generic contract so local dev is unchanged. Bypass\n * still requires the explicit VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true opt-in.\n */\nfunction fromBuildEnv(): DataqAuthConfig {\n  const tenantId = import.meta.env.VITE_AZURE_TENANT_ID;\n  const clientId = import.meta.env.VITE_AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID;\n  const apiClientId = import.meta.env.VITE_AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID;\n  const scope = import.meta.env.VITE_AZURE_API_SCOPE || 'user_impersonation';\n  const bypass = import.meta.env.VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS === 'true';\n  return {\n    mode: bypass ? 'bypass' : tenantId && clientId ? 'oidc' : undefined,\n    authority: tenantId ? `https://login.microsoftonline.com/${tenantId}/v2.0` : undefined,\n    clientId: clientId || undefined,\n    apiScope: apiClientId ? `api://${apiClientId}/${scope}` : undefined,\n  };\n}\n\n// The injected runtime config wins; the build-time env is the dev-only fallback\n// used only when no /config.js was served (i.e. `pnpm dev`).\nconst injected = typeof window !== 'undefined' ? window.__DATAQ_CONFIG__?.auth : undefined;\nconst cfg: DataqAuthConfig = injected ?? fromBuildEnv();\n\nexport const authConfig = {\n  authority: cfg.authority,\n  clientId: cfg.clientId,\n  apiScope: cfg.apiScope,\n} as const;\n\nexport const authMode: AuthMode = (() => {\n  // Fail-closed: bypass ONLY on the explicit flag, never inferred.\n  if (cfg.mode === 'bypass') return 'dev_bypass';\n  if (cfg.authority && cfg.clientId) return 'real';\n  return 'unconfigured';\n})();\n\nexport const DEV_USER = {\n  name: 'Dev Bypass User',\n  username: 'dev-bypass@dataq.local',\n  homeAccountId: 'dev-bypass',\n  isDev: true as const,\n};\n"

1	# DataQ frontend image — build the Vite SPA, serve the static dist via nginx.
2	# Build context = frontend/ :  docker build -f frontend/Dockerfile frontend/
3	#
4	# NOTE: Azure Static Web App serves dist/ directly and does NOT need this image
5	# (the deploy workflow builds + uploads dist to SWA). This Dockerfile is the
6	# container option — e.g. running the UI on Container Apps behind the same
7	# ingress as the API — and keeps the UI deployable without Azure-specific glue.
8	#
9	# VITE_* values are inlined at build time (Vite bakes them into the bundle), so
10	# they're build args, not runtime env. Pass them with --build-arg.
11	#
12	# Two published variants share this one Dockerfile (#472):
13	#   :latest — production build (BUILD_NODE_ENV=production, no dev-bypass). For
14	#             real-auth self-host: pass your VITE_AZURE_* at build time.
15	#   :dev    — zero-config eval image: BUILD_NODE_ENV=development (so
16	#             import.meta.env.DEV is true → the dev-bypass auth gate in
17	#             src/auth/config.ts activates) + VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true. No
18	#             Azure tenant needed; what docker-compose.ghcr.yml pulls.
19	
20	FROM node:22-alpine AS build
21	WORKDIR /app
22	RUN corepack enable
23	
24	COPY package.json pnpm-lock.yaml ./
25	RUN pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
26	
27	COPY . .
28	ARG VITE_AZURE_TENANT_ID=""
29	ARG VITE_AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID=""
30	ARG VITE_AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID=""
31	ARG VITE_AZURE_API_SCOPE="user_impersonation"
32	ARG VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS="false"
33	# Vite ties import.meta.env.DEV/PROD to NODE_ENV (NOT to --mode), so the eval
34	# image builds with BUILD_NODE_ENV=development to make DEV true; the default
35	# production build keeps DEV false (the auth-bypass gate stays inert).
36	ARG BUILD_NODE_ENV="production"
37	ENV VITE_AZURE_TENANT_ID=$VITE_AZURE_TENANT_ID \
38	    VITE_AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID=$VITE_AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID \
39	    VITE_AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID=$VITE_AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID \
40	    VITE_AZURE_API_SCOPE=$VITE_AZURE_API_SCOPE \
41	    VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=$VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS
42	RUN NODE_ENV=$BUILD_NODE_ENV pnpm build
43	
44	FROM nginx:1.27-alpine AS serve
45	# Link the GHCR package to this repo (shows under the repo's Packages, lets the
46	# repo's Actions GITHUB_TOKEN push it, and inherits anonymous-pull visibility —
47	# ADR 0023, mirrors backend/Dockerfile).
48	LABEL org.opencontainers.image.source="https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ"
49	LABEL org.opencontainers.image.description="DataQ frontend (React SPA served by nginx)"
50	LABEL org.opencontainers.image.licenses="MIT"
51	COPY --from=build /app/dist /usr/share/nginx/html
52	# Template (not a static conf): the nginx entrypoint envsubst's it at startup so
53	# the API upstream is configurable. Default targets the compose `api` service.
54	COPY nginx.conf.template /etc/nginx/templates/default.conf.template
55	ENV DATAQ_API_UPSTREAM=http://api:8000
56	EXPOSE 8080
57

Auth config is injected at RUNTIME — nginx serves /config.js from\n# the DATAQ_AUTH_* env below (envsubst at startup), and the SPA reads it before\n# the bundle runs. So the same image serves the eval stack (DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=bypass)\n# and a real deployment (DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=oidc + authority/clientId/scope) — set the\n# env at `docker run`, no rebuild. Replaces the #472 two-image (:latest/:dev) split.\n#\n# NOTE: the deploy workflow currently builds dist/ and uploads to Static Web App;\n# ADR 0028 moves the deployed frontend onto this container (SWA can't inject\n# runtime config).\n\nFROM node:22-alpine AS build\nWORKDIR /app\nRUN corepack enable\n\nCOPY package.json pnpm-lock.yaml ./\nRUN pnpm install --frozen-lockfile\n\nCOPY . .\nRUN pnpm build\n\nFROM nginx:1.27-alpine AS serve\n# Link the GHCR package to this repo (shows under the repo's Packages, lets the\n# repo's Actions GITHUB_TOKEN push it, and inherits anonymous-pull visibility —\n# ADR 0023, mirrors backend/Dockerfile).\nLABEL org.opencontainers.image.source=\"https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ\"\nLABEL org.opencontainers.image.description=\"DataQ frontend (React SPA served by nginx)\"\nLABEL org.opencontainers.image.licenses=\"MIT\"\nCOPY --from=build /app/dist /usr/share/nginx/html\n# Template (not a static conf): the nginx entrypoint envsubst's it at startup so\n# the API upstream + auth config are runtime-configurable.\nCOPY nginx.conf.template /etc/nginx/templates/default.conf.template\n# Runtime config env (ADR 0028) — MUST be defined (even if empty) so envsubst\n# always substitutes them in /config.js; empty → SPA is unconfigured (fail-closed),\n# bypass needs an explicit DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=bypass. DATAQ_API_UPSTREAM defaults to\n# the compose `api` service.\nENV DATAQ_API_UPSTREAM=http://api:8000 \\\n    DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=\"\" \\\n    DATAQ_AUTH_AUTHORITY=\"\" \\\n    DATAQ_AUTH_CLIENT_ID=\"\" \\\n    DATAQ_AUTH_API_SCOPE=\"\"\nEXPOSE 8080"

42	jobs:
43	  publish:
44	    name: Build + push ${{ matrix.name }} ${{ matrix.variant }} (amd64 + arm64)
45	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
46	    strategy:
47	      fail-fast: false
48	      matrix:
49	        include:
50	          # Backend build context is the repo ROOT (the app imports as the
51	          # top-level `backend.app.*` package — see backend/Dockerfile). Its auth
52	          # mode is a runtime env var, so one image serves every deployment.
53	          - name: backend
54	            variant: standard
55	            dockerfile: backend/Dockerfile
56	            context: .
57	            build_args: ""
58	          # Frontend build context is frontend/ (its Dockerfile COPYs from there).
59	          # The SPA bakes auth mode at build time, so it ships as TWO images:
60	          #   standard → :latest (+ sha / release tag): production build, no
61	          #              bypass. Real-auth self-host rebuilds with their VITE_AZURE_*.
62	          - name: frontend
63	            variant: standard
64	            dockerfile: frontend/Dockerfile
65	            context: frontend
66	            build_args: ""
67	          #   dev → :dev only: NODE_ENV=development (→ import.meta.env.DEV true, so
68	          #         the dev-bypass auth gate activates) + VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true.
69	          #         The zero-config eval image docker-compose.ghcr.yml pulls.
70	          - name: frontend
71	            variant: dev
72	            dockerfile: frontend/Dockerfile
73	            context: frontend
74	            build_args: |
75	              BUILD_NODE_ENV=development
76	              VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true
77	    steps:
78	      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
79	
80	      # QEMU provides the arm64 emulation the amd64 runner needs to build the
81	      # non-native platform; buildx drives the multi-platform build + manifest.
82	      - uses: docker/setup-qemu-action@v3
83	      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
84	
85	      - name: Log in to GHCR
86	        uses: docker/login-action@v4
87	        with:
88	          registry: ghcr.io
89	          username: ${{ github.actor }}
90	          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
91	
92	      - name: Compute image tags
93	        id: tags
94	        # Untrusted inputs come in via env (never interpolated into the script
95	        # body) so a dispatch `tag` value can't inject shell — IMAGE_NAME / VARIANT
96	        # are static matrix values, INPUT_TAG the user-supplied one.
97	        env:
98	          IMAGE_NAME: ${{ matrix.name }}
99	          VARIANT: ${{ matrix.variant }}
100	          INPUT_TAG: ${{ inputs.tag }}
101	        run: |
102	          set -euo pipefail
103	          image="${REGISTRY}/${OWNER}/dataq-${IMAGE_NAME}"
104	          if [ "${VARIANT}" = "dev" ]; then
105	            # The dev-bypass eval variant owns a single moving tag (:dev). It must
106	            # NOT write :latest/:sha — those are the production build's pointers.
107	            tags="${image}:dev"
108	          else
109	            # Standard build: the moving stable pointer + the immutable commit SHA.
110	            tags="${image}:latest"$'\n'"${image}:${GITHUB_SHA}"
111	            # On a release-tag push, github.ref_name is the tag (vX.Y.Z); on a
112	            # manual run, the optional `tag` input. Publish it as a third tag.
113	            extra="${INPUT_TAG}"
114	            if [ -z "$extra" ] && [ "${GITHUB_REF_TYPE}" = "tag" ]; then
115	              extra="${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"
116	            fi
117	            # Validate the extra tag against Docker's tag grammar (alphanumerics +
118	            # _.- , ≤128 chars, no leading separator) before it reaches the ref.
119	            if [ -n "$extra" ] && ! printf '%s' "$extra" | grep -Eq '^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,127}$'; then
120	              echo "::error::Invalid image tag '${extra}' — must match Docker's tag grammar."
121	              exit 1
122	            fi
123	            if [ -n "$extra" ]; then
124	              tags="${tags}"$'\n'"${image}:${extra}"
125	            fi
126	          fi
127	          echo "Publishing tags:"; echo "$tags"
128	          # Multi-line output for the build-push-action `tags:` list.
129	          {
130	            echo "tags<<EOF"
131	            echo "$tags"
132	            echo "EOF"
133	          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
134	
135	      - name: Build + push (multi-arch)
136	        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
137	        with:
138	          context: ${{ matrix.context }}
139	          file: ${{ matrix.dockerfile }}
140	          build-args: ${{ matrix.build_args }}
141	          platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64

> AGENT

I reviewed the full diff across all angles. I've already browser-verified the happy paths, so I focused on edge cases and removed guards. **One real finding — a removed safety guard:**

**`config.ts` `fromBuildEnv()` dropped the `import.meta.env.DEV` gate on dev-bypass.** The old code was `import.meta.env.DEV && devBypass` — so a *production* build could never enable bypass. The new `fromBuildEnv` gates bypass only on `VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS === 'true'`, no DEV check. That matters because `fromBuildEnv` is **not** dead in production: the **SWA deploy** (still live until the stage-4 cutover) serves the static bundle, where `/config.js` is the stub that doesn't set the global → `fromBuildEnv` runs and reads the baked `VITE_*`. So a static/SWA build with `VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true` baked would now enable auth-bypass in production, where the old DEV guard prevented it. It's mitigated only by `deploy.yml` hard-coding `false` — a lost belt-and-suspenders. Cheap fix: restore the DEV gate (image path is unaffected — it never uses `fromBuildEnv`).

Let me apply it.

The image path never\n  // reaches here (nginx injects window.__DATAQ_CONFIG__).\n  const bypass = import.meta.env.DEV && import.meta.env.VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS === 'true';"

import { MsalProvider as ReactMsalProvider } from '@azure/msal-react';
import type { ReactNode } from 'react';

import { getMsalInstance } from './msalInstance';

/**
 * Wraps children in MSAL's React provider when running in real auth mode.
 * In dev_bypass / unconfigured modes, this is a passthrough — no MsalProvider
 * is mounted, so useMsal()-using components must not be rendered (handled by
 * CurrentUserProvider and AuthGate dispatching by mode).
 */
export function MsalProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  const instance = getMsalInstance();
  if (!instance) return <>{children}</>;
  return <ReactMsalProvider instance={instance}>{children}</ReactMsalProvider>;
}

import { StrictMode } from 'react';
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client';
import { App as AntApp, ConfigProvider } from 'antd';
import { BrowserRouter } from 'react-router-dom';

import { App } from './App';
import { CurrentUserProvider } from './auth/CurrentUserProvider';
import { MeProvider } from './auth/MeProvider';
import { MsalProvider } from './auth/MsalProvider';
import { getMsalInstance } from './auth/msalInstance';
import { ErrorBoundary } from './components/ErrorBoundary';
import { appTheme } from './theme';
// Self-hosted fonts (visual-fidelity pass, ADR 0022) — Inter for UI text,
// JetBrains Mono for code/SQL/identifiers. Bundled via @fontsource (no external
// CDN fetch, clears pnpm audit). Only the weights the design uses, and only the
// **latin** subset — the UI is English; shipping cyrillic/greek/vietnamese
// subsets would balloon the SWA asset count for glyphs we never render (a stray
// non-latin data value just falls back to the system font). Imported before
// styles.css so the @font-face rules register ahead of our overrides.
import '@fontsource/inter/latin-400.css';
import '@fontsource/inter/latin-500.css';
import '@fontsource/inter/latin-600.css';
import '@fontsource/inter/latin-700.css';
import '@fontsource/jetbrains-mono/latin-400.css';
import '@fontsource/jetbrains-mono/latin-500.css';
import './styles.css';

const maybeRoot = document.getElementById('root');
if (!maybeRoot) {
  throw new Error('Root element #root not found in index.html');
}
const rootEl: HTMLElement = maybeRoot;

// MSAL lifecycle (issue #62):
//   1. .initialize() must complete before any MSAL API call (v5 requirement).
//   2. .handleRedirectPromise() must resolve before React renders so the
//      first paint reflects post-login state.
//   3. Errors surface to the console + a static page — fail loud during dev.
async function bootstrap() {
  const instance = getMsalInstance();
  if (instance) {
    await instance.initialize();
    await instance.handleRedirectPromise();
  }
  createRoot(rootEl).render(
    <StrictMode>
      <ConfigProvider theme={appTheme}>
        <AntApp>
          <ErrorBoundary>
            <MsalProvider>
              <CurrentUserProvider>
                <MeProvider>
                  <BrowserRouter>
                    <App />
                  </BrowserRouter>
                </MeProvider>
              </CurrentUserProvider>
            </MsalProvider>
          </ErrorBoundary>
        </AntApp>
      </ConfigProvider>
    </StrictMode>,
  );
}

bootstrap().catch((err) => {
  console.error('MSAL bootstrap failed', err);
  rootEl.innerHTML =
    '<pre style="padding:24px;color:#a00">Authentication bootstrap failed. See console.</pre>';
});

  "content": "import { UserManager, WebStorageStateStore, type User } from 'oidc-client-ts';\n\nimport { authConfig, authMode } from './config';\n\n/**\n * Generic OIDC auth client (ADR 0028 / #504) — replaces the Azure-specific MSAL\n * client. Any standards-compliant IdP works: Azure AD, Cognito, GCP Identity\n * Platform, Keycloak, or a local dev OIDC — the provider is just the injected\n * `authority`. Authorization-code + PKCE (oidc-client-ts default), refresh-token\n * silent renew (offline_access), session-storage cache (matches the old MSAL\n * choice so a tab reload keeps the session but a closed tab drops it).\n */\n\nlet _mgr: UserManager | null = null;\n\n/**\n * The UserManager singleton in real auth mode; null in dev_bypass / unconfigured.\n * Caller awaits nothing to construct it — oidc-client-ts fetches the IdP metadata\n * lazily on first sign-in/callback.\n */\nexport function getUserManager(): UserManager | null {\n  if (authMode !== 'real') return null;\n  if (_mgr) return _mgr;\n\n  const { authority, clientId, apiScope } = authConfig;\n  if (!authority || !clientId) {\n    // authMode='real' guarantees both are set; defensive guard satisfies the type checker.\n    throw new Error('Real auth mode requires an authority + clientId (DATAQ_AUTH_* runtime config)');\n  }\n\n  // openid/profile/email → id token; offline_access → refresh token for silent\n  // renew; apiScope (when set) makes the access token audience the DataQ API.\n  const scope = ['openid', 'profile', 'email', 'offline_access', apiScope]\n    .filter(Boolean)\n    .join(' ');\n\n  _mgr = new UserManager({\n    authority,\n    client_id: clientId,\n    // Trailing slash matches the registered SPA redirect URI (Azure AD requires a\n    // trailing slash when the URI has no path segment — see deploy/terraform/sso.tf).\n    redirect_uri: `${window.location.origin}/`,\n    post_logout_redirect_uri: `${window.location.origin}/`,\n    scope,\n    automaticSilentRenew: true,\n    userStore: new WebStorageStateStore({ store: window.sessionStorage }),\n  });\n  return _mgr;\n}\n\n/** Begin an interactive sign-in (full-page redirect to the IdP). */\nexport async function login(): Promise<void> {\n  const mgr = getUserManager();\n  if (mgr) await mgr.signinRedirect();\n}\n\n/** End the session (redirect to the IdP's logout, then back). */\nexport async function logout(): Promise<void> {\n  const mgr = getUserManager();\n  if (mgr) await mgr.signoutRedirect();\n}\n\n/** True when the current URL is the IdP redirect back (has an auth code + state). */\nfunction isSigninCallback(): boolean {\n  const params = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search);\n  return params.has('code') && params.has('state');\n}\n\n/**\n * Bootstrap step: if this load is the sign-in redirect back, complete the code\n * exchange and scrub the code/state from the URL (so a reload doesn't replay it).\n * No-op otherwise. Must run before React renders so the first paint is post-login.\n */\nexport async function completeSigninIfCallback(): Promise<void> {\n  const mgr = getUserManager();\n  if (!mgr || !isSigninCallback()) return;\n  await mgr.signinRedirectCallback();\n  window.history.replaceState({}, document.title, window.location.pathname);\n}\n\n/**\n * A currently-valid API access token, or null when not signed in. Refreshes\n * silently when the cached token is missing/expired; if that needs user\n * interaction (expired session / revoked consent / fresh MFA), falls back to an\n * interactive redirect and rejects so the in-flight request doesn't fire\n * tokenless — it re-issues cleanly once the redirect completes (was #168).\n */\nexport async function getApiToken(): Promise<string | null> {\n  const mgr = getUserManager();\n  if (!mgr) return null;\n  const user = await mgr.getUser();\n  if (user && !user.expired) return user.access_token;\n  try {\n    const renewed = await mgr.signinSilent();\n    return renewed?.access_token ?? null;\n  } catch (err) {\n    await mgr.signinRedirect();\n    throw err;\n  }\n}\n\n/** Test-only: drop the cached UserManager so the next call rebuilds it. */\nexport function resetAuthClientCache(): void {\n  _mgr = null;\n}\n\nexport type { User };\n"
}

  "content": "import { createContext, useContext, useEffect, useState, type ReactNode } from 'react';\n\nimport { getUserManager, type User } from './authClient';\n\n/**\n * Subscribes to the OIDC UserManager and exposes the signed-in user to the tree\n * (the generic-client replacement for msal-react's MsalProvider + useMsal). In\n * dev_bypass / unconfigured modes getUserManager() is null, so this is a\n * passthrough with a null user — CurrentUserProvider and AuthGate dispatch by\n * auth mode, so nothing reads the user in those modes.\n */\n\ninterface AuthState {\n  user: User | null;\n}\n\nconst AuthContext = createContext<AuthState>({ user: null });\n\nexport function AuthProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {\n  const mgr = getUserManager();\n  const [user, setUser] = useState<User | null>(null);\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    if (!mgr) return;\n    let active = true;\n    // Seed from any persisted session, then track load/unload (sign-in, silent\n    // renew, sign-out) so the tree re-renders on session changes.\n    void mgr.getUser().then((u) => {\n      if (active) setUser(u);\n    });\n    const onLoaded = (u: User) => setUser(u);\n    const onUnloaded = () => setUser(null);\n    mgr.events.addUserLoaded(onLoaded);\n    mgr.events.addUserUnloaded(onUnloaded);\n    return () => {\n      active = false;\n      mgr.events.removeUserLoaded(onLoaded);\n      mgr.events.removeUserUnloaded(onUnloaded);\n    };\n  }, [mgr]);\n\n  return <AuthContext.Provider value={{ user }}>{children}</AuthContext.Provider>;\n}\n\n/** The current OIDC user (null when not signed in / not in real auth mode). */\nexport function useAuthUser(): User | null {\n  return useContext(AuthContext).user;\n}\n"
}

2	import axios, { type AxiosError, type InternalAxiosRequestConfig } from 'axios';
