4	import { authConfig, authMode } from '../auth/config';
5	import { getMsalInstance } from '../auth/msalInstance';
6	
7	/**
8	 * Shared axios instance for DataQ API calls.
9	 *
10	 * baseURL is relative (/api/v1); vite dev proxy forwards to the FastAPI
11	 * backend on :8000, and production same-origin deploy needs no CORS.
12	 *
13	 * Request interceptor attaches an Azure AD bearer token in real auth mode.
14	 * In dev_bypass / unconfigured modes the interceptor is a no-op (backend
15	 * dev-bypass resolves the user without a token).
16	 *
17	 * When the silent refresh can't complete without user interaction (expired
18	 * session / revoked consent / fresh MFA — surfaced by MSAL as
19	 * InteractionRequiredAuthError) the interceptor falls back to an interactive
20	 * redirect. That navigates the browser to Azure AD, so the in-flight request is
21	 * aborted (rejected) — it re-issues cleanly once MSAL completes the redirect
22	 * handshake on the way back.
23	 *
24	 * Response interceptor surfaces the DataQ error envelope's human message
25	 * (`{ error: { code, message, detail } }`) as `error.message`, so callers'
26	 * `err.message` shows the actionable backend reason instead of axios's generic
27	 * "Request failed with status code 4xx".
28	 */
29	export const api = axios.create({
30	  baseURL: '/api/v1',
31	});
32	
33	api.interceptors.request.use(attachBearerToken);
34	
35	api.interceptors.response.use(
36	  (response) => response,
37	  (error: AxiosError<{ error?: { message?: string } }>) => {
38	    const apiMessage = error.response?.data?.error?.message;
39	    if (apiMessage) error.message = apiMessage;
40	    return Promise.reject(error);
41	  },
42	);
43	
44	async function attachBearerToken(
45	  config: InternalAxiosRequestConfig,
46	): Promise<InternalAxiosRequestConfig> {
47	  if (authMode !== 'real') return config;
48	  const instance = getMsalInstance();
49	  if (!instance) return config;
50	  const account = instance.getAllAccounts()[0];
51	  if (!account || !authConfig.apiScope) return config;
52	
53	  const scopes = [authConfig.apiScope];
54	  try {
55	    const result = await instance.acquireTokenSilent({ account, scopes });
56	    config.headers.set('Authorization', `Bearer ${result.accessToken}`);
57	    return config;
58	  } catch (err) {
59	    if (err instanceof InteractionRequiredAuthError) {
60	      // Silent refresh can't proceed without the user — hand off to an
61	      // interactive redirect (consistent with AuthGate's loginRedirect). This
62	      // navigates away; reject so the in-flight request doesn't fire tokenless.
63	      await instance.acquireTokenRedirect({ account, scopes });
64	    }
65	    throw err;
66	  }
67	}

Silent renew and the interactive-redirect\n * fallback (when the session needs the user again — expired / revoked consent /\n * fresh MFA) live in getApiToken(); on that redirect the in-flight request is\n * aborted (rejected) and re-issues cleanly after the handshake (was #168).\n *\n * Response interceptor surfaces the DataQ error envelope's human message\n * (`{ error: { code, message, detail } }`) as `error.message`, so callers'\n * `err.message` shows the actionable backend reason instead of axios's generic\n * \"Request failed with status code 4xx\".\n */\nexport const api = axios.create({\n  baseURL: '/api/v1',\n});\n\napi.interceptors.request.use(attachBearerToken);\n\napi.interceptors.response.use(\n  (response) => response,\n  (error: AxiosError<{ error?: { message?: string } }>) => {\n    const apiMessage = error.response?.data?.error?.message;\n    if (apiMessage) error.message = apiMessage;\n    return Promise.reject(error);\n  },\n);\n\nasync function attachBearerToken(\n  config: InternalAxiosRequestConfig,\n): Promise<InternalAxiosRequestConfig> {\n  if (authMode !== 'real') return config;\n  const token = await getApiToken();\n  if (token) config.headers.set('Authorization', `Bearer ${token}`);\n  return config;\n}"
}

21	function RealAuthGate({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
22	  const isAuthenticated = useIsAuthenticated();
23	  const { instance, inProgress } = useMsal();
24	
25	  if (isAuthenticated) return <>{children}</>;
26

28	    void instance.loginRedirect({
29	      scopes: authConfig.apiScope ? [authConfig.apiScope] : [],
30	    });
31	  };

34	  // reachable states are Startup (brief boot) and HandleRedirect (the sign-in
35	  // redirect handshake) — both are genuinely "auth in progress", so a plain
36	  // !== None is correct here. (Logout / AcquireToken don't occur pre-auth, and
37	  // this MSAL version's InteractionStatus has no Login member.)
38	  const signingIn = inProgress !== InteractionStatus.None;
39	
40	  return <LoginPage onSignIn={onSignIn} signingIn={signingIn} />;
41	}

{

  "content": "import { useEffect, useState, type ReactNode } from 'react';\n\nimport { getUserManager, type User } from './authClient';\nimport { AuthContext } from './authContext';\n\n/**\n * Subscribes to the OIDC UserManager and exposes the signed-in user to the tree\n * (the generic-client replacement for msal-react's MsalProvider + useMsal). In\n * dev_bypass / unconfigured modes getUserManager() is null, so this is a\n * passthrough with a null user — CurrentUserProvider and AuthGate dispatch by\n * auth mode, so nothing reads the user in those modes.\n */\nexport function AuthProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {\n  const mgr = getUserManager();\n  const [user, setUser] = useState<User | null>(null);\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    if (!mgr) return;\n    let active = true;\n    // Seed from any persisted session, then track load/unload (sign-in, silent\n    // renew, sign-out) so the tree re-renders on session changes.\n    void mgr.getUser().then((u) => {\n      if (active) setUser(u);\n    });\n    const onLoaded = (u: User) => setUser(u);\n    const onUnloaded = () => setUser(null);\n    mgr.events.addUserLoaded(onLoaded);\n    mgr.events.addUserUnloaded(onUnloaded);\n    return () => {\n      active = false;\n      mgr.events.removeUserLoaded(onLoaded);\n      mgr.events.removeUserUnloaded(onUnloaded);\n    };\n  }, [mgr]);\n\n  return <AuthContext.Provider value={{ user }}>{children}</AuthContext.Provider>;\n}\n"
}

The line-by-line agent returned 6 findings; I'm waiting on the removed-behavior/cross-file agent before applying fixes together. My initial read on the 6:

- **Valid, will fix:** (1) `isSigninCallback` ignores IdP **error** redirects (`?error=…` with no `code`) — failures get stuck; (2) `getApiToken` calls `signinSilent` even when `getUser()` is null → hits the iframe path with no `silent_redirect_uri` → unhandled rejection; (4) no in-flight **dedup** — concurrent expired requests fire multiple silent renews/redirects; (6) `AuthProvider` ignores `silentRenewError`/`userSignedOut` → stale "signed-in" UI after a failed background renew.
- **Not a stage-2 regression (defer):** (3) deep-link lost after login — MSAL's `loginRedirect` did the same, so it's a pre-existing limitation, not new.
- **Keeping as-is:** (5) `invalid_grant` in the interaction set — that's the correct signal for an expired refresh token; the config-loop scenario would surface at first login, not here.

## #504 stage 2 — MSAL → generic OIDC client (PR #508)

1	# Static Web App — hosts the React/Vite build. Standard SKU so the api Container
2	# App can be linked as a backend: SWA then proxies /api/* to it same-origin, which
3	# is exactly what frontend/public/staticwebapp.config.json + the relative axios baseURL
4	# ('/api/v1') expect (no CORS). The SPA content is uploaded by the Deploy workflow
5	# (Azure/static-web-apps-deploy) using the api token output below.
6	
7	resource "azurerm_static_web_app" "app" {
8	  name                = "dataq-app-web"
9	  resource_group_name = data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name
10	  location            = var.azure_location
11	  sku_tier            = var.swa_sku
12	  sku_size            = var.swa_sku
13	  tags                = local.common_tags
14	
15	  depends_on = [azurerm_resource_provider_registration.web]
16	}
17	
18	# Link the api Container App as the SWA backend. No azurerm resource covers
19	# arbitrary linked backends (only the Functions registration), so use the CLI.
20	#
21	# `backends link` errors if *any* backend is already linked, so we can't just
22	# `|| true` — that would also mask a real failure (bad region, missing
23	# permission) AND still record the trigger hash as applied, so the broken link
24	# is reported as success and never retried (#396). Instead: check the current
25	# link state first and skip only when our api is already the linked backend;
26	# any other failure from `link` propagates (set -e, no swallow). Re-run after
27	# changing the api by tainting this resource.
28	resource "null_resource" "swa_linked_backend" {
29	  triggers = {
30	    swa_id = azurerm_static_web_app.app.id
31	    api_id = azurerm_container_app.api.id
32	  }
33	  provisioner "local-exec" {
34	    interpreter = ["/bin/bash", "-c"]
35	    command     = <<-CMD
36	      set -euo pipefail
37	      # Substring-match the api's resource id against the raw `show` output rather
38	      # than a JMESPath: the exact JSON shape of `backends show` (array vs object,
39	      # flattened vs `properties`-nested) is version-dependent, but the full
40	      # resource id is unique enough that finding it anywhere means it's linked.
41	      # `|| true` covers the no-backend-linked case (empty/non-zero) without
42	      # masking the link step below. A *different* backend linked (only one is
43	      # allowed) won't match, so we fall through to link and that fails loudly.
44	      linked=$(az staticwebapp backends show \
45	        --name ${azurerm_static_web_app.app.name} \
46	        --resource-group ${data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name} \
47	        --only-show-errors -o json || true)
48	      if printf '%s' "$linked" | grep -qF "${azurerm_container_app.api.id}"; then
49	        echo "api already linked as the SWA backend — skipping"
50	        exit 0
51	      fi
52	      az staticwebapp backends link \
53	        --name ${azurerm_static_web_app.app.name} \
54	        --resource-group ${data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name} \
55	        --backend-resource-id ${azurerm_container_app.api.id} \
56	        --backend-region ${data.azurerm_container_app_environment.shared.location} \
57	        --only-show-errors --output none
58	    CMD
59	  }
60	  depends_on = [azurerm_static_web_app.app, azurerm_container_app.api]
61	}
62

1	# The DataQ backend on Container Apps — api (external ingress), worker (Celery +
2	# embedded beat), and the migrate Job. All three run the SAME GHCR image
3	# (ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-backend:<tag>), pulled anonymously (public
4	# package, ADR 0023 — no registry block / credential).
5	#
6	# Boot-critical secrets (DATABASE_URL, App Insights) are inline Container App
7	# secrets, NOT KV references (see keyvault.tf for why). REDIS_URL is non-secret
8	# (in-environment, no auth). The app's runtime SecretStore reads datasource creds
9	# from Key Vault via the attached user-assigned identity (SECRET_STORE +
10	# AZURE_KEY_VAULT_URL).
11	
12	locals {
13	  backend_image   = "${var.backend_image_repo}:${var.image_tag}"
14	  azure_tenant_id = var.azure_tenant_id != "" ? var.azure_tenant_id : data.azurerm_client_config.current.tenant_id
15	
16	  # Inline secrets shared by api + worker (+ DATABASE_URL also on the migrate job).
17	  app_secrets = [
18	    { name = "database-url", value = local.database_url },
19	    { name = "redis-url", value = local.redis_url },
20	    { name = "appinsights-conn", value = azurerm_application_insights.app.connection_string },
21	  ]
22	
23	  # Non-secret env + secret_name references, shared by api + worker.
24	  app_env = [
25	    { name = "ENVIRONMENT", value = var.environment },
26	    { name = "LOG_LEVEL", value = "INFO" },
27	    { name = "DATABASE_URL", secret_name = "database-url" },
28	    { name = "REDIS_URL", secret_name = "redis-url" },
29	    { name = "APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING", secret_name = "appinsights-conn" },
30	    { name = "SAMPLE_FAILURES_RETENTION_DAYS", value = "30" },
31	    # Runtime SecretStore -> Key Vault via the user-assigned identity.
32	    { name = "SECRET_STORE", value = "azure_key_vault" },
33	    { name = "AZURE_KEY_VAULT_URL", value = azurerm_key_vault.app.vault_uri },
34	    # DefaultAzureCredential can't select a USER-assigned identity without being
35	    # told which one. Without this, every Key Vault read fails (no MI chosen) —
36	    # breaking secret resolution for connection tests, suite runs, and the
37	    # orchestration poll (#406). Must be the UAMI's client id, not principal id.
38	    { name = "AZURE_CLIENT_ID", value = azurerm_user_assigned_identity.app.client_id },
39	    # Real SSO in prod (AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=false). Client IDs come from the SSO app
40	    # registrations created in sso.tf; init_auth() validates v2 tokens against
41	    # AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID + AZURE_TENANT_ID.
42	    { name = "AUTH_DEV_BYPASS", value = "false" },
43	    { name = "AZURE_TENANT_ID", value = local.azure_tenant_id },
44	    { name = "AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID", value = azuread_application.api.client_id },
45	    { name = "AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID", value = azuread_application.spa.client_id },
46	    { name = "AZURE_API_SCOPE", value = var.azure_api_scope },
47	    # Guest (B2B / external) sign-in. Off by default (secure); this deployment
48	    # opts in via tfvars because the owner signs in with a guest account. When
49	    # off, the token validator rejects guests with 403 "Guest users not allowed".
50	    { name = "AZURE_ALLOW_GUEST_USERS", value = var.azure_allow_guest_users ? "true" : "false" },
51	    { name = "WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS", value = var.workspace_admin_emails },
52	    # Empty: the SWA linked backend proxies /api same-origin, so the FastAPI CORS
53	    # middleware stays off (README §4 / ADR 0018).
54	    { name = "CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS", value = "" },
55	    # Public origin for the inbound-webhook URLs the admin webhook-config surface
56	    # generates (#490). The SWA host proxies /api same-origin, so an orchestrator
57	    # POSTing to <swa>/api/v1/orchestration/events/... reaches the api.
58	    { name = "PUBLIC_BASE_URL", value = "https://${azurerm_static_web_app.app.default_host_name}" },
59	    # Webhook secret KEY names (values live in Key Vault — keyvault.tf).
60	    { name = "ADF_WEBHOOK_SECRET_NAME", value = "adf-webhook-secret" },
61	    { name = "AIRFLOW_WEBHOOK_SECRET_NAME", value = "airflow-webhook-secret" },
62	    # Alerting channels (Slack + email) behind the ResultPublisher composite.
63	    # Secret NAMES point at Key Vault (the webhook URL / app-password live there);
64	    # SMTP coordinates are non-secret. Each publisher self-no-ops until its secret
65	    # + (for email) recipients are set, so leaving the email_* vars empty = email
66	    # off. Email addresses come from the gitignored tfvars (PII, not in git).
67	    { name = "SLACK_WEBHOOK_SECRET_NAME", value = "channel-slack-webhook" },
68	    { name = "EMAIL_SMTP_HOST", value = "smtp.gmail.com" },
69	    { name = "EMAIL_SMTP_PORT", value = "587" },
70	    { name = "EMAIL_PASSWORD_SECRET_NAME", value = "channel-email-password" },
71	    { name = "EMAIL_USERNAME", value = var.email_username },
72	    { name = "EMAIL_FROM", value = var.email_from },
73	    { name = "EMAIL_TO", value = var.email_to },
74	  ]
75	}
76	
77	# ── API (FastAPI, external ingress) ──────────────────────────────────────────
78	resource "azurerm_container_app" "api" {
79	  name                         = "dataq-app-api"
80	  container_app_environment_id = data.azurerm_container_app_environment.shared.id
81	  resource_group_name          = data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name
82	  revision_mode                = "Single"
83	
84	  identity {
85	    type         = "UserAssigned"
86	    identity_ids = [azurerm_user_assigned_identity.app.id]
87	  }
88	
89	  dynamic "secret" {
90	    for_each = local.app_secrets
91	    content {
92	      name  = secret.value.name
93	      value = secret.value.value
94	    }
95	  }
96	
97	  ingress {
98	    external_enabled = true
99	    target_port      = 8000
100	    transport        = "auto"
101	    traffic_weight {
102	      latest_revision = true
103	      percentage      = 100
104	    }
105	  }
106	
107	  template {
108	    min_replicas = 1
109	    max_replicas = 3
110	    container {
111	      name   = "api"
112	      image  = local.backend_image
113	      cpu    = 0.5
114	      memory = "1Gi"
115	      # Image CMD already runs `uvicorn backend.app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0
116	      # --port 8000` (no --reload in the image), so no command override.
117	      dynamic "env" {
118	        for_each = local.app_env
119	        content {
120	          name        = env.value.name
121	          value       = lookup(env.value, "value", null)
122	          secret_name = lookup(env.value, "secret_name", null)
123	        }
124	      }
125	    }
126	  }
127	
128	  tags       = local.common_tags
129	  depends_on = [azurerm_role_assignment.kv_app_reader]
130	}
131	
132	# ── Worker (Celery worker + embedded beat) ───────────────────────────────────
133	resource "azurerm_container_app" "worker" {
134	  name                         = "dataq-app-worker"
135	  container_app_environment_id = data.azurerm_container_app_environment.shared.id
136	  resource_group_name          = data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name
137	  revision_mode                = "Single"
138	
139	  identity {
140	    type         = "UserAssigned"
141	    identity_ids = [azurerm_user_assigned_identity.app.id]
142	  }
143	
144	  dynamic "secret" {
145	    for_each = local.app_secrets
146	    content {
147	      name  = secret.value.name
148	      value = secret.value.value
149	    }
150	  }
151	
152	  template {
153	    # min_replicas = 1: the worker also runs celery-beat (-B) for the schedule
154	    # dispatcher + orchestration polling, so it can't scale to zero.
155	    min_replicas = 1
156	    max_replicas = 1
157	    container {
158	      name    = "worker"
159	      image   = local.backend_image
160	      cpu     = 1.0
161	      memory  = "2Gi"
162	      command = ["celery", "-A", "backend.app.worker.celery_app", "worker", "-B", "--loglevel=INFO"]
163	      dynamic "env" {
164	        for_each = local.app_env
165	        content {
166	          name        = env.value.name
167	          value       = lookup(env.value, "value", null)
168	          secret_name = lookup(env.value, "secret_name", null)
169	        }
170	      }
171	    }
172	  }
173	
174	  tags       = local.common_tags
175	  depends_on = [azurerm_role_assignment.kv_app_reader]
176	}
177	
178	# ── Migrate Job (alembic upgrade head) ───────────────────────────────────────
179	# Manual-trigger job the Deploy workflow runs BEFORE rolling the apps (additive,
180	# backward-compatible migrations — CLAUDE.md). alembic.ini's script_location is
181	# relative to backend/, so cd there first (mirrors docker-compose's migrate svc).
182	resource "azurerm_container_app_job" "migrate" {
183	  name                         = "dataq-app-migrate"
184	  container_app_environment_id = data.azurerm_container_app_environment.shared.id
185	  resource_group_name          = data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name
186	  # A Container Apps Job must be in the same region as its (shared) environment.
187	  location = data.azurerm_container_app_environment.shared.location
188	
189	  replica_timeout_in_seconds = 900
190	  replica_retry_limit        = 1
191	
192	  manual_trigger_config {
193	    parallelism              = 1
194	    replica_completion_count = 1
195	  }
196	
197	  secret {
198	    name  = "database-url"
199	    value = local.database_url
200	  }
201	
202	  template {
203	    container {
204	      name    = "migrate"
205	      image   = local.backend_image
206	      cpu     = 0.5
207	      memory  = "1Gi"
208	      command = ["sh", "-c", "cd backend && alembic upgrade head"]
209	      env {
210	        name        = "DATABASE_URL"
211	        secret_name = "database-url"
212	      }
213	    }
214	  }
215	
216	  tags = local.common_tags
217	}
218

1	# Azure AD SSO app registrations (real auth in prod; AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=false). The
2	# backend's init_auth() requires AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID + AZURE_TENANT_ID at startup
3	# and validates v2 access tokens; the SPA (MSAL) uses AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID with a
4	# redirect URI of the SWA origin. Two registrations:
5	#   - API  (dataq-app-api-sso): exposes the `user_impersonation` scope, v2 tokens.
6	#   - SPA  (dataq-app-spa): public single-page client, redirect = SWA origin,
7	#                           pre-authorized on the API scope (no consent prompt).
8	
9	data "azuread_client_config" "current" {}
10	
11	resource "random_uuid" "api_scope" {}
12	
13	# ── API app registration ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
14	resource "azuread_application" "api" {
15	  display_name = "dataq-app-api-sso"
16	  owners       = [data.azuread_client_config.current.object_id]
17	
18	  api {
19	    requested_access_token_version = 2 # v2 tokens (login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/v2.0)
20	
21	    oauth2_permission_scope {
22	      id                         = random_uuid.api_scope.result
23	      value                      = var.azure_api_scope
24	      type                       = "User"
25	      enabled                    = true
26	      admin_consent_display_name = "Access the DataQ API"
27	      admin_consent_description  = "Allow the application to access the DataQ API on behalf of the signed-in user."
28	      user_consent_display_name  = "Access the DataQ API"
29	      user_consent_description   = "Allow the application to access the DataQ API on your behalf."
30	    }
31	  }
32	}
33	
34	# api://<client_id> identifier URI (separate resource — needs the client_id known).
35	resource "azuread_application_identifier_uri" "api" {
36	  application_id = azuread_application.api.id
37	  identifier_uri = "api://${azuread_application.api.client_id}"
38	}
39	
40	resource "azuread_service_principal" "api" {
41	  client_id = azuread_application.api.client_id
42	  owners    = [data.azuread_client_config.current.object_id]
43	}
44	
45	# ── SPA app registration ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
46	resource "azuread_application" "spa" {
47	  display_name = "dataq-app-spa"
48	  owners       = [data.azuread_client_config.current.object_id]
49	
50	  single_page_application {
51	    # Azure AD requires a trailing slash when there's no path segment; the SPA's
52	    # MSAL redirectUri is set to `${window.location.origin}/` to match exactly
53	    # (frontend/src/auth/msalInstance.ts).
54	    redirect_uris = ["https://${azurerm_static_web_app.app.default_host_name}/"]
55	  }
56	
57	  # Request the API's user_impersonation scope.
58	  required_resource_access {
59	    resource_app_id = azuread_application.api.client_id
60	    resource_access {
61	      id   = random_uuid.api_scope.result
62	      type = "Scope"
63	    }
64	  }
65	
66	  # Microsoft Graph User.Read (sign-in + read profile).
67	  required_resource_access {
68	    resource_app_id = "00000003-0000-0000-c000-000000000000"
69	    resource_access {
70	      id   = "e1fe6dd8-ba31-4d61-89e7-88639da4683d" # User.Read
71	      type = "Scope"
72	    }
73	  }
74	}
75	
76	resource "azuread_service_principal" "spa" {
77	  client_id = azuread_application.spa.client_id
78	  owners    = [data.azuread_client_config.current.object_id]
79	}
80	
81	# Pre-authorize the SPA on the API scope so users aren't prompted to consent to
82	# the custom API (same-tenant, single product).
83	resource "azuread_application_pre_authorized" "spa_on_api" {
84	  application_id       = azuread_application.api.id
85	  authorized_client_id = azuread_application.spa.client_id
86	  permission_ids       = [random_uuid.api_scope.result]
87	}
88

1	name: Deploy
2	
3	# Manual-only for now (workflow_dispatch): apply-ready scaffolding that never
4	# fires on its own until the Azure resources exist + secrets/vars are set. Once
5	# the infra is provisioned (see deploy/README.md), flip on the push trigger:
6	#   push:
7	#     branches: [main]
8	on:
9	  workflow_dispatch:
10	    inputs:
11	      image_tag:
12	        description: "Image tag to build + deploy (blank → the commit SHA, an immutable tag)"
13	        default: ""
14	
15	concurrency:
16	  group: deploy-production
17	  cancel-in-progress: false
18	
19	# OIDC federated login to Azure (no stored client secret). The federated cred +
20	# the listed vars/secrets must be configured first — see deploy/README.md.
21	# packages:write lets the GITHUB_TOKEN push the backend image to GHCR (ADR 0023).
22	permissions:
23	  id-token: write
24	  contents: read
25	  packages: write
26	
27	env:
28	  # GHCR registry (ADR 0023) — public package, lowercase owner. ACA pulls it
29	  # anonymously, so no registry credential is stored on the apps/job.
30	  #
31	  # Default the tag to the commit SHA (#382): `latest` is mutable, so a push
32	  # racing the deploy could make the migrate job, API, and worker each resolve a
33	  # *different* image; the SHA tag is immutable, so all three roll the exact
34	  # build this run produced. A manual `image_tag` input still overrides it. On a
35	  # push:[main] trigger `inputs` is empty, so it falls back to the SHA too.
36	  IMAGE: ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-backend:${{ inputs.image_tag || github.sha }}
37	
38	jobs:
39	  backend:
40	    name: Backend — build, migrate, deploy (API + worker)
41	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
42	    environment: production
43	    steps:
44	      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
45	
46	      - name: Azure login (OIDC)
47	        uses: azure/login@v3
48	        with:
49	          client-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
50	          tenant-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
51	          subscription-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}
52	
53	      # Push to GHCR (ADR 0023). The GITHUB_TOKEN has packages:write on this repo's
54	      # registry; no Azure/ACR credential is involved in the image push.
55	      - name: Log in to GHCR
56	        uses: docker/login-action@v4
57	        with:
58	          registry: ghcr.io
59	          username: ${{ github.actor }}
60	          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
61	
62	      - name: Build + push backend image to GHCR
63	        run: |
64	          docker build -f backend/Dockerfile -t "$IMAGE" .
65	          docker push "$IMAGE"
66	
67	      # Migrate BEFORE rolling the app: migrations are additive/backward-compatible
68	      # (CLAUDE.md), so the running old code tolerates the new schema. Runs the
69	      # one-off migrate Container Apps Job (provisioned per deploy/README.md).
70	      # `az containerapp job start` only *starts* the execution and returns, so we
71	      # capture the execution name and poll it to a terminal state — the rollout
72	      # below must not begin until the migration has actually SUCCEEDED, and a
73	      # failed migration must abort the deploy (fail-closed) rather than roll the
74	      # apps onto an un-migrated schema.
75	      - name: Run DB migrations (alembic upgrade head) and wait for success
76	        run: |
77	          set -euo pipefail
78	          # Roll the job's image on the template FIRST, then start it with no
79	          # --image override. Passing --image to `job start` replaces the
80	          # container template without the Terraform-configured command
81	          # (`sh -c "cd backend && alembic upgrade head"`), so the execution
82	          # falls back to the image's default CMD (uvicorn) and never migrates.
83	          # Updating the template preserves that command (mirrors the api/worker
84	          # `az containerapp update --image` steps below).
85	          az containerapp job update \
86	            --name "${{ vars.MIGRATE_JOB_NAME }}" \
87	            --resource-group "${{ vars.AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
88	            --image "$IMAGE"
89	          exec_name=$(az containerapp job start \
90	            --name "${{ vars.MIGRATE_JOB_NAME }}" \
91	            --resource-group "${{ vars.AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
92	            --query name -o tsv)
93	          echo "Started migration execution: $exec_name"
94	          # Poll to a terminal state. Besides the 15-min wall-clock cap, bound the
95	          # number of *consecutive* empty/unexpected statuses: a control-plane
96	          # hiccup or a CLI status-field rename would otherwise leave the loop
97	          # polling a status it never recognises until the full deadline, tying up
98	          # the prod concurrency group with no signal (#397). A recognised
99	          # in-progress status resets the counter; `|| true` keeps a transient
100	          # query failure a retry (counted as unknown) rather than a hard step
101	          # abort under `set -e`.
102	          deadline=$(( SECONDS + 900 ))  # 15-minute cap
103	          unknown=0
104	          unknown_max=18  # ~3 min of consecutive empty/unexpected status → abort
105	          while (( SECONDS < deadline )); do
106	            status=$(az containerapp job execution list \
107	              --name "${{ vars.MIGRATE_JOB_NAME }}" \
108	              --resource-group "${{ vars.AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
109	              --query "[?name=='$exec_name'].properties.status | [0]" -o tsv 2>/dev/null || true)
110	            echo "migration status: ${status:-<pending>} (unknown streak: $unknown)"
111	            case "$status" in
112	              Succeeded) echo "Migration succeeded."; exit 0 ;;
113	              Failed|Degraded|Stopped) echo "::error::Migration $status — aborting before app rollout."; exit 1 ;;
114	              Running|Processing|Pending) unknown=0 ;;
115	              *)
116	                unknown=$(( unknown + 1 ))
117	                if (( unknown >= unknown_max )); then
118	                  echo "::error::Migration status empty/unexpected ('${status:-<empty>}') $unknown times in a row — aborting before app rollout."
119	                  exit 1
120	                fi
121	                ;;
122	            esac
123	            sleep 10
124	          done
125	          echo "::error::Timed out waiting for migration to complete."; exit 1
126	
127	      - name: Deploy API
128	        run: |
129	          az containerapp update \
130	            --name "${{ vars.API_APP_NAME }}" \
131	            --resource-group "${{ vars.AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
132	            --image "$IMAGE"
133	
134	      - name: Deploy worker
135	        run: |
136	          az containerapp update \
137	            --name "${{ vars.WORKER_APP_NAME }}" \
138	            --resource-group "${{ vars.AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
139	            --image "$IMAGE"
140	
141	  frontend:
142	    name: Frontend — build + deploy to Static Web App
143	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
144	    environment: production
145	    # Gate on the backend (build → migrate → roll API/worker): a failed/aborted
146	    # migration must stop the UI deploy, else a new SPA rolls against an un-rolled
147	    # or half-migrated API — a partial deploy (#382).
148	    needs: backend
149	    steps:
150	      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
151	      # version is required: action-setup runs at the repo root, whose
152	      # package.json has no `packageManager` field (it lives in frontend/).
153	      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6
154	        with:
155	          version: 9.15.4
156	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
157	        with:
158	          node-version: "22"
159	          cache: pnpm
160	          cache-dependency-path: frontend/pnpm-lock.yaml
161	
162	      - name: Build
163	        working-directory: frontend
164	        # VITE_* are inlined at build time. Non-secret azure client/tenant ids
165	        # come from repo vars; never the SPA secret (there is none — MSAL is public).
166	        env:
167	          VITE_AZURE_TENANT_ID: ${{ vars.VITE_AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
168	          VITE_AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.VITE_AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID }}
169	          VITE_AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.VITE_AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID }}
170	          VITE_AZURE_API_SCOPE: ${{ vars.VITE_AZURE_API_SCOPE }}
171	          VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS: "false"
172	        run: |
173	          pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
174	          pnpm build
175	
176	      - name: Deploy to Azure Static Web Apps
177	        uses: Azure/static-web-apps-deploy@v1
178	        with:
179	          azure_static_web_apps_api_token: ${{ secrets.AZURE_STATIC_WEB_APPS_API_TOKEN }}
180	          action: upload
181	          app_location: frontend/dist
182	          skip_app_build: true
183	
```

1	# DataQ frontend image — build the Vite SPA, serve the static dist via nginx.
2	# Build context = frontend/ :  docker build -f frontend/Dockerfile frontend/
3	#
4	# ONE generic image, nothing baked in (ADR 0028): no cloud, no secret, no
5	# auth-bypass. Auth config is injected at RUNTIME — nginx serves /config.js from
6	# the DATAQ_AUTH_* env below (envsubst at startup), and the SPA reads it before
7	# the bundle runs. So the same image serves the eval stack (DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=bypass)
8	# and a real deployment (DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=oidc + authority/clientId/scope) — set the
9	# env at `docker run`, no rebuild. Replaces the #472 two-image (:latest/:dev) split.
10	#
11	# NOTE: the deploy workflow currently builds dist/ and uploads to Static Web App;
12	# ADR 0028 moves the deployed frontend onto this container (SWA can't inject
13	# runtime config).
14	
15	FROM node:22-alpine AS build
16	WORKDIR /app
17	RUN corepack enable
18	
19	COPY package.json pnpm-lock.yaml ./
20	RUN pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
21	
22	COPY . .
23	RUN pnpm build
24	
25	FROM nginx:1.27-alpine AS serve
26	# Link the GHCR package to this repo (shows under the repo's Packages, lets the
27	# repo's Actions GITHUB_TOKEN push it, and inherits anonymous-pull visibility —
28	# ADR 0023, mirrors backend/Dockerfile).
29	LABEL org.opencontainers.image.source="https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ"
30	LABEL org.opencontainers.image.description="DataQ frontend (React SPA served by nginx)"
31	LABEL org.opencontainers.image.licenses="MIT"
32	COPY --from=build /app/dist /usr/share/nginx/html
33	# Template (not a static conf): the nginx entrypoint envsubst's it at startup so
34	# the API upstream + auth config are runtime-configurable.
35	COPY nginx.conf.template /etc/nginx/templates/default.conf.template
36	# Runtime config env (ADR 0028) — MUST be defined (even if empty) so envsubst
37	# always substitutes them in /config.js; empty → SPA is unconfigured (fail-closed),
38	# bypass needs an explicit DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=bypass. DATAQ_API_UPSTREAM defaults to
39	# the compose `api` service.
40	ENV DATAQ_API_UPSTREAM=http://api:8000 \
41	    DATAQ_AUTH_MODE="" \
42	    DATAQ_AUTH_AUTHORITY="" \
43	    DATAQ_AUTH_CLIENT_ID="" \
44	    DATAQ_AUTH_API_SCOPE=""
45	EXPOSE 8080
46

1	# Serve the built SPA AND reverse-proxy the API + MCP to the backend, so the
2	# prebuilt UI image works same-origin without Azure Static Web App "linking"
3	# (the no-clone `docker compose -f docker-compose.ghcr.yml up` path — #472).
4	#
5	# This is a TEMPLATE: the nginx image's entrypoint runs envsubst over
6	# /etc/nginx/templates/*.template at startup, so ${DATAQ_API_UPSTREAM} is filled
7	# from the env (default http://api:8000, set in frontend/Dockerfile; overridable
8	# in compose). Only env vars that are actually set are substituted, so nginx's
9	# own $uri / $host / $scheme runtime vars are left untouched.
10	server {
11	    listen 8080;
12	    server_name _;
13	    root /usr/share/nginx/html;
14	    index index.html;
15	
16	    # Runtime app config (ADR 0028). Rendered from DATAQ_AUTH_* env by the same
17	    # startup envsubst, served BEFORE the app bundle so the SPA reads it
18	    # synchronously (window.__DATAQ_CONFIG__). One generic image, nothing baked.
19	    # This exact-match location wins over the static /config.js stub in the bundle.
20	    # Empty values → the SPA treats auth as unconfigured (fail-closed); dev-bypass
21	    # requires an explicit DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=bypass. no-cache so a restart with new
22	    # env takes effect. (Auth values are URLs/ids/scopes — no single-quote/$ to
23	    # break the returned string.)
24	    location = /config.js {
25	        default_type application/javascript;
26	        add_header Cache-Control "no-cache";
27	        return 200 'window.__DATAQ_CONFIG__={"auth":{"mode":"${DATAQ_AUTH_MODE}","authority":"${DATAQ_AUTH_AUTHORITY}","clientId":"${DATAQ_AUTH_CLIENT_ID}","apiScope":"${DATAQ_AUTH_API_SCOPE}"}};';
28	    }
29	
30	    # Docker Compose's embedded DNS. Resolving the upstream through a variable
31	    # (below) defers DNS to request time, so this image starts even while the api
32	    # service is still coming up and survives an api container restart (new IP) —
33	    # a literal proxy_pass host is resolved once at startup and would hard-crash
34	    # nginx if api isn't up yet.
35	    resolver 127.0.0.11 ipv6=off valid=10s;
36	
37	    # REST API — same-origin /api/* forwarded to the backend. proxy_pass uses a
38	    # variable, so the original URI isn't auto-appended; $request_uri carries the
39	    # full path + query (/api/v1/...) through unchanged.
40	    location /api/ {
41	        set $dataq_upstream "${DATAQ_API_UPSTREAM}";
42	        proxy_pass $dataq_upstream$request_uri;
43	        proxy_set_header Host $host;
44	        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
45	        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
46	        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
47	    }
48	
49	    # MCP sub-app (FastMCP at /mcp). Streamable-HTTP/SSE needs HTTP/1.1 with no
50	    # response buffering and no hop-by-hop Connection header, or events stall.
51	    location /mcp {
52	        set $dataq_upstream "${DATAQ_API_UPSTREAM}";
53	        proxy_pass $dataq_upstream$request_uri;
54	        proxy_http_version 1.1;
55	        proxy_set_header Connection "";
56	        proxy_buffering off;
57	        proxy_set_header Host $host;
58	        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
59	        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
60	        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
61	    }
62	
63	    # Long-cache fingerprinted assets; never cache index.html (it points at the
64	    # current asset hashes).
65	    location /assets/ {
66	        try_files $uri =404;
67	        expires 1y;
68	        add_header Cache-Control "public, immutable";
69	    }
70	
71	    # SPA fallback: any non-file path returns index.html so client-side routes
72	    # (deep links like /results/:runId) resolve to the app.
73	    location / {
74	        try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html;
75	        add_header Cache-Control "no-cache";
76	    }
77	}
78	
```

2	# capped at ONE Container App Environment, so we do NOT create one here — the
3	# harness Terraform owns it (renamed to the neutral `dataq-cae`). The app stack

6	# the app's container resources land there too.

1	# Shared data sources, locals, and the idempotent RG ensure-step.
2	
3	data "azurerm_client_config" "current" {}
4	
5	data "azurerm_subscription" "current" {}
6	
7	# ── Idempotent RG step ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
8	# `az group create` is idempotent: it creates dataq-rg if absent and is a no-op
9	# (with the same tags) if it already exists. We only ever pass project=dataq so
10	# the shared RG's existing tag is preserved and the harness resources in the same
11	# RG are unaffected. The data source below then references the (now-guaranteed) RG
12	# — we never manage/destroy the shared RG as a Terraform resource.
13	resource "null_resource" "ensure_rg" {
14	  triggers = {
15	    rg       = var.azure_resource_group
16	    location = var.azure_location
17	  }
18	  provisioner "local-exec" {
19	    command = "az group create --name ${var.azure_resource_group} --location '${var.azure_location}' --tags project=dataq --only-show-errors --output none"
20	  }
21	}
22	
23	data "azurerm_resource_group" "dataq" {
24	  name       = var.azure_resource_group
25	  depends_on = [null_resource.ensure_rg]
26	}
27	
28	resource "random_string" "suffix" {
29	  length  = 6
30	  lower   = true
31	  upper   = false
32	  numeric = true
33	  special = false
34	}
35	
36	locals {
37	  # All DataQ-APP resources carry purpose=dataq-app so they're trivially
38	  # distinguishable from the harness's purpose=dataq-harness resources in the
39	  # shared RG (see the verification query in deploy/terraform/README.md).
40	  common_tags = {
41	    project = var.project_tag
42	    managed = "terraform"
43	    purpose = "dataq-app"
44	  }
45	}
46

1	name: Publish images (GHCR, multi-arch)
2	
3	# Builds + publishes the BYOL distribution images to GHCR — multi-arch
4	# (linux/amd64 + linux/arm64) so Apple-Silicon devs pull a native image, not an
5	# emulated one (#472). ADR 0023 (GHCR is the BYOL registry) / ADR 0013.
6	#
7	# This is DELIBERATELY separate from deploy.yml: that workflow builds an
8	# amd64-only, SHA-tagged BACKEND image for the Azure rollout (ACA is amd64, the
9	# immutable SHA tag is correct there). This one publishes BOTH images, multi-arch,
10	# under a moving `:latest` stable pointer for `docker compose ... up`-from-image
11	# users. The two never both fire on the same event (deploy is manual-dispatch).
12	#
13	# Stable tag to pull = `:latest` (moving). The immutable per-deploy `:vN` backend
14	# tags (v7, v10, …) stay owned by deploy.yml — this workflow never writes them.
15	# A release-tag push (vX.Y.Z) additionally publishes that semver tag.
16	
17	on:
18	  workflow_dispatch:
19	    inputs:
20	      tag:
21	        description: "Extra immutable tag to publish alongside :latest + the commit SHA (e.g. v1.0.0). Blank → just :latest + SHA."
22	        default: ""
23	  push:
24	    tags:
25	      - "v*"
26	
27	concurrency:
28	  group: publish-images
29	  cancel-in-progress: false
30	
31	# GITHUB_TOKEN needs packages:write to push to the repo-linked GHCR packages
32	# (ADR 0023). No Azure/registry credential is involved.
33	permissions:
34	  contents: read
35	  packages: write
36	
37	env:
38	  REGISTRY: ghcr.io
39	  # Lowercase owner — GHCR paths are case-sensitive and must be lowercase.
40	  OWNER: theurgicduke771
41	
42	jobs:
43	  publish:
44	    name: Build + push ${{ matrix.name }} (amd64 + arm64)
45	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
46	    strategy:
47	      fail-fast: false
48	      matrix:
49	        include:
50	          # Backend build context is the repo ROOT (the app imports as the
51	          # top-level `backend.app.*` package — see backend/Dockerfile).
52	          - name: backend
53	            dockerfile: backend/Dockerfile
54	            context: .
55	          # Frontend build context is frontend/ (its Dockerfile COPYs from there).
56	          # One generic image (ADR 0028) — auth mode is injected at runtime, so no
57	          # build-args and no per-variant image; the same :latest serves eval + prod.
58	          - name: frontend
59	            dockerfile: frontend/Dockerfile
60	            context: frontend
61	    steps:
62	      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
63	
64	      # QEMU provides the arm64 emulation the amd64 runner needs to build the
65	      # non-native platform; buildx drives the multi-platform build + manifest.
66	      - uses: docker/setup-qemu-action@v3
67	      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
68	
69	      - name: Log in to GHCR
70	        uses: docker/login-action@v4
71	        with:
72	          registry: ghcr.io
73	          username: ${{ github.actor }}
74	          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
75	
76	      - name: Compute image tags
77	        id: tags
78	        # Untrusted inputs come in via env (never interpolated into the script
79	        # body) so a dispatch `tag` value can't inject shell — IMAGE_NAME is the
80	        # static matrix name, INPUT_TAG the user-supplied one.
81	        env:
82	          IMAGE_NAME: ${{ matrix.name }}
83	          INPUT_TAG: ${{ inputs.tag }}
84	        run: |
85	          set -euo pipefail
86	          image="${REGISTRY}/${OWNER}/dataq-${IMAGE_NAME}"
87	          # The moving stable pointer + the immutable commit SHA.
88	          tags="${image}:latest"$'\n'"${image}:${GITHUB_SHA}"
89	          # On a release-tag push, github.ref_name is the tag (vX.Y.Z); on a
90	          # manual run, the optional `tag` input. Publish it as a third tag.
91	          extra="${INPUT_TAG}"
92	          if [ -z "$extra" ] && [ "${GITHUB_REF_TYPE}" = "tag" ]; then
93	            extra="${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"
94	          fi
95	          # Validate the extra tag against Docker's tag grammar (alphanumerics +
96	          # _.- , ≤128 chars, no leading separator) before it reaches the ref.
97	          if [ -n "$extra" ] && ! printf '%s' "$extra" | grep -Eq '^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,127}$'; then
98	            echo "::error::Invalid image tag '${extra}' — must match Docker's tag grammar."
99	            exit 1
100	          fi
101	          if [ -n "$extra" ]; then
102	            tags="${tags}"$'\n'"${image}:${extra}"
103	          fi
104	          echo "Publishing tags:"; echo "$tags"
105	          # Multi-line output for the build-push-action `tags:` list.
106	          {
107	            echo "tags<<EOF"
108	            echo "$tags"
109	            echo "EOF"
110	          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

1	/**
2	 * Auth configuration — sourced at RUNTIME, not build time (ADR 0028).
3	 *
4	 * The container serves `/config.js` (rendered from env by nginx at startup) which
5	 * sets `window.__DATAQ_CONFIG__` before the app bundle runs. That means one
6	 * generic image with nothing baked in — no cloud, no secret, no auth-bypass.
7	 * When no such global is present — `pnpm dev`, and the static/SWA build until the
8	 * ADR-0028 cutover — we fall back to the build-time `VITE_*` env (bypass there
9	 * stays DEV-gated, so a production static bundle can't enable it).
10	 *
11	 * The injected contract is provider-neutral (`DATAQ_AUTH_*`): `mode` + a standard
12	 * OIDC-shaped `authority` / `clientId` / `apiScope`. Azure is one populated shape
13	 * (`authority = https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/v2.0`); no `AZURE` in
14	 * the contract.
15	 *
16	 * Mode is computed once at module load:
17	 * - 'real'         — `mode:'oidc'` with authority + clientId present. The auth
18	 *                    client (MSAL today; a generic OIDC client next — #504) drives
19	 *                    redirect-flow login + token acquisition.
20	 * - 'dev_bypass'   — ONLY when `mode:'bypass'` is explicitly set. Fail-closed:
21	 *                    never inferred from missing config. Renders a fixed dev user.
22	 * - 'unconfigured' — anything else. AuthGate shows a setup-needed banner.
23	 */
24	
25	export type AuthMode = 'real' | 'dev_bypass' | 'unconfigured';
26	
27	/** The runtime auth contract injected via `window.__DATAQ_CONFIG__.auth`. */
28	export interface DataqAuthConfig {
29	  /** 'bypass' = no IdP (local/eval); 'oidc' = real sign-in. Absent → unconfigured. */
30	  mode?: 'bypass' | 'oidc';
31	  /** OIDC issuer/authority URL (e.g. https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/v2.0). */
32	  authority?: string;
33	  /** The public SPA client id registered with the IdP. */
34	  clientId?: string;
35	  /** Full scope string requested for the API access token (Azure: api://<api-client-id>/<scope>). */
36	  apiScope?: string;
37	}
38	
39	declare global {
40	  interface Window {
41	    __DATAQ_CONFIG__?: { auth?: DataqAuthConfig };
42	  }
43	}
44	
45	/**
46	 * Build-time fallback for `pnpm dev` (no injected /config.js). Maps the legacy
47	 * VITE_* Azure vars onto the generic contract so local dev is unchanged. Bypass
48	 * still requires the explicit VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true opt-in.
49	 */
50	function fromBuildEnv(): DataqAuthConfig {
51	  const tenantId = import.meta.env.VITE_AZURE_TENANT_ID;
52	  const clientId = import.meta.env.VITE_AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID;
53	  const apiClientId = import.meta.env.VITE_AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID;
54	  const scope = import.meta.env.VITE_AZURE_API_SCOPE || 'user_impersonation';
55	  // Belt-and-suspenders: bypass in the build-env fallback stays gated on a DEV
56	  // build, so a production static bundle (e.g. the SWA deploy, which serves this
57	  // fallback path — the /config.js stub sets no global) can never enable auth
58	  // bypass even if VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true were baked in. The image path never
59	  // reaches here (nginx injects window.__DATAQ_CONFIG__).
60	  const bypass = import.meta.env.DEV && import.meta.env.VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS === 'true';
61	  return {
62	    mode: bypass ? 'bypass' : tenantId && clientId ? 'oidc' : undefined,
63	    authority: tenantId ? `https://login.microsoftonline.com/${tenantId}/v2.0` : undefined,
64	    clientId: clientId || undefined,
65	    apiScope: apiClientId ? `api://${apiClientId}/${scope}` : undefined,
66	  };
67	}
68	
69	// The injected runtime config wins; the build-time env is the dev-only fallback
70	// used only when no /config.js was served (i.e. `pnpm dev`).
71	const injected = typeof window !== 'undefined' ? window.__DATAQ_CONFIG__?.auth : undefined;
72	const cfg: DataqAuthConfig = injected ?? fromBuildEnv();
73	
74	export const authConfig = {
75	  authority: cfg.authority,
76	  clientId: cfg.clientId,
77	  apiScope: cfg.apiScope,
78	} as const;
79	
80	export const authMode: AuthMode = (() => {
81	  // Fail-closed: bypass ONLY on the explicit flag, never inferred.
82	  if (cfg.mode === 'bypass') return 'dev_bypass';
83	  if (cfg.authority && cfg.clientId) return 'real';
84	  return 'unconfigured';
85	})();
86	
87	export const DEV_USER = {
88	  name: 'Dev Bypass User',
89	  username: 'dev-bypass@dataq.local',
90	  homeAccountId: 'dev-bypass',
91	  isDev: true as const,
92	};
93	
```

I have the full picture now. Key design decisions for the scaffold:

- **Break the TF circular dependency** (frontend needs api's FQDN as upstream; api needs frontend's FQDN for `PUBLIC_BASE_URL`/SPA redirect) by computing both FQDNs from the shared env's `default_domain` instead of referencing each other's resources.
- **Make the nginx resolver cloud-neutral** — auto-detect from `/etc/resolv.conf` (works for compose's `127.0.0.11` AND ACA/K8s cluster DNS) instead of the hardcoded Docker resolver, which would break in ACA.
- **Fix upstream Host/SNI** for the external-FQDN api so ACA's Envoy routes correctly, without breaking the compose path.

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/frontend/docker-entrypoint.d/15-dataq-resolver.envsh",
  "content": "# Auto-detect the DNS resolver from /etc/resolv.conf so the templated proxy_pass\n# upstream (a hostname resolved at REQUEST time — see nginx.conf.template) works\n# in ANY runtime without baking a cloud-specific resolver IP into the image\n# (ADR 0028 — one cloud-neutral image):\n#   - Docker Compose  → embedded DNS at 127.0.0.11\n#   - Azure Container Apps / Kubernetes → the in-cluster DNS nameserver\n# A literal `resolver 127.0.0.11` (the compose default) is WRONG in ACA and makes\n# every /api proxy fail DNS. Detecting it per-runtime keeps the image generic.\n#\n# `.envsh` (not `.sh`) so the nginx entrypoint SOURCES this — the export must\n# reach 20-envsubst-on-templates.sh, which renders ${DATAQ_DNS_RESOLVER} into the\n# conf. Runs before 20- (lexical order). Override by setting DATAQ_DNS_RESOLVER\n# explicitly (detection is skipped when it's already set).\nif [ -z \"${DATAQ_DNS_RESOLVER:-}\" ]; then\n    DATAQ_DNS_RESOLVER=\"$(awk '/^nameserver/ { print $2; exit }' /etc/resolv.conf 2>/dev/null)\"\n    # Fall back to the compose embedded-DNS address if resolv.conf had no entry.\n    : \"${DATAQ_DNS_RESOLVER:=127.0.0.11}\"\n    export DATAQ_DNS_RESOLVER\n    echo \"dataq: using DNS resolver ${DATAQ_DNS_RESOLVER} for proxy upstreams\"\nfi\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/deploy/terraform/frontend.tf",
  "content": "# DataQ frontend on Container Apps (ADR 0028 §5 cutover — replaces the Static Web\n# App, swa.tf). ONE generic nginx image (ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-frontend),\n# pulled anonymously (public GHCR package, ADR 0023). Nothing is baked in: the SPA\n# auth config + the /api proxy upstream are injected at RUNTIME via the DATAQ_*\n# env below (nginx envsubst → /config.js + the proxy_pass upstream). This is why\n# SWA couldn't host it — a static host can't inject runtime config.\n#\n# External ingress on 8080. The nginx conf reverse-proxies /api + /mcp to the api\n# Container App (same-origin, no CORS — the api keeps CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS empty),\n# so this app is the single public product surface; the api stays externally\n# reachable too (Azure Monitor→ADF webhook posts to PUBLIC_BASE_URL/api/...).\n\nresource \"azurerm_container_app\" \"frontend\" {\n  name                         = \"dataq-app-frontend\"\n  container_app_environment_id = data.azurerm_container_app_environment.shared.id\n  resource_group_name          = data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name\n  revision_mode                = \"Single\"\n\n  ingress {\n    external_enabled = true\n    target_port      = 8080\n    transport        = \"auto\"\n    traffic_weight {\n      latest_revision = true\n      percentage      = 100\n    }\n  }\n\n  template {\n    min_replicas = 1\n    max_replicas = 2\n    container {\n      name   = \"frontend\"\n      image  = \"${var.frontend_image_repo}:${var.frontend_image_tag}\"\n      cpu    = 0.25\n      memory = \"0.5Gi\"\n\n      # Proxy upstream — the api Container App's public FQDN (computed from the env\n      # domain to avoid a resource cycle; see local.api_public_url). nginx sends\n      # the matching Host + TLS SNI so ACA's Envoy routes it to the api.\n      env {\n        name  = \"DATAQ_API_UPSTREAM\"\n        value = local.api_public_url\n      }\n\n      # Runtime auth config (generic DATAQ_AUTH_* contract, ADR 0028). Real OIDC\n      # against Azure AD: mode=oidc + the SPA client + the tenant v2 authority +\n      # the full API scope. Validated end-to-end against this exact tenant in the\n      # #504 stage-3 pass. `mode=oidc` (anything != \"bypass\") keeps bypass OFF.\n      env {\n        name  = \"DATAQ_AUTH_MODE\"\n        value = \"oidc\"\n      }\n      env {\n        name  = \"DATAQ_AUTH_AUTHORITY\"\n        value = \"https://login.microsoftonline.com/${local.azure_tenant_id}/v2.0\"\n      }\n      env {\n        name  = \"DATAQ_AUTH_CLIENT_ID\"\n        value = azuread_application.spa.client_id\n      }\n      # Full scope string the SPA requests for the API access token\n      # (api://<api-client-id>/<scope>), per the config.ts apiScope contract.\n      env {\n        name  = \"DATAQ_AUTH_API_SCOPE\"\n        value = \"api://${azuread_application.api.client_id}/${var.azure_api_scope}\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  tags = local.common_tags\n}\n"
}

{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/.github/workflows/deploy.yml",
  "old_string": "  frontend:\n    name: Frontend — build + deploy to Static Web App\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    environment: production\n    # Gate on the backend (build → migrate → roll API/worker): a failed/aborted\n    # migration must stop the UI deploy, else a new SPA rolls against an un-rolled\n    # or half-migrated API — a partial deploy (#382).\n    needs: backend\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@v7\n      # version is required: action-setup runs at the repo root, whose\n      # package.json has no `packageManager` field (it lives in frontend/).\n      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6\n        with:\n          version: 9.15.4\n      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6\n        with:\n          node-version: \"22\"\n          cache: pnpm\n          cache-dependency-path: frontend/pnpm-lock.yaml\n\n      - name: Build\n        working-directory: frontend\n        # VITE_* are inlined at build time. Non-secret azure client/tenant ids\n        # come from repo vars; never the SPA secret (there is none — MSAL is public).\n        env:\n          VITE_AZURE_TENANT_ID: ${{ vars.VITE_AZURE_TENANT_ID }}\n          VITE_AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.VITE_AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID }}\n          VITE_AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.VITE_AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID }}\n          VITE_AZURE_API_SCOPE: ${{ vars.VITE_AZURE_API_SCOPE }}\n          VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS: \"false\"\n        run: |\n          pnpm install --frozen-lockfile\n          pnpm build\n\n      - name: Deploy to Azure Static Web Apps\n        uses: Azure/static-web-apps-deploy@v1\n        with:\n          azure_static_web_apps_api_token: ${{ secrets.AZURE_STATIC_WEB_APPS_API_TOKEN }}\n          action: upload\n          app_location: frontend/dist\n          skip_app_build: true",
  "new_string": "  frontend:\n    name: Frontend — build image, deploy to Container App\n    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    environment: production\n    # Gate on the backend (build → migrate → roll API/worker): a failed/aborted\n    # migration must stop the UI deploy, else a new SPA rolls against an un-rolled\n    # or half-migrated API — a partial deploy (#382).\n    needs: backend\n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@v7\n\n      - name: Azure login (OIDC)\n        uses: azure/login@v3\n        with:\n          client-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}\n          tenant-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}\n          subscription-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}\n\n      - name: Log in to GHCR\n        uses: docker/login-action@v4\n        with:\n          registry: ghcr.io\n          username: ${{ github.actor }}\n          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}\n\n      # One generic image (ADR 0028) — nothing baked in. Auth config + the /api\n      # proxy upstream are injected at runtime by the Container App env\n      # (DATAQ_AUTH_* / DATAQ_API_UPSTREAM in deploy/terraform/frontend.tf), so\n      # there are NO VITE_* build args here and no per-environment rebuild. amd64\n      # only (ACA is amd64); the multi-arch :latest is published by\n      # publish-images.yml for the BYOL/eval path.\n      - name: Build + push frontend image to GHCR\n        run: |\n          docker build -f frontend/Dockerfile -t \"$IMAGE_FRONTEND\" frontend\n          docker push \"$IMAGE_FRONTEND\"\n\n      - name: Deploy frontend\n        run: |\n          az containerapp update \\\n            --name \"${{ vars.FRONTEND_APP_NAME }}\" \\\n            --resource-group \"${{ vars.AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP }}\" \\\n            --image \"$IMAGE_FRONTEND\""
}

```
1	# GitHub Actions -> Azure auth for the Deploy workflow (.github/workflows/deploy.yml)
2	# via OIDC federated credentials — no stored client secret. The workflow's
3	# azure/login uses the client/tenant/subscription ids output by this stack; the SP
4	# gets Contributor on dataq-rg so it can run `az containerapp update` / `job start`
5	# (the GHCR image push uses the workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN, not this SP).
6	
7	resource "azuread_application" "github_deploy" {
8	  display_name = "dataq-github-deploy"
9	}
10	
11	resource "azuread_service_principal" "github_deploy" {
12	  client_id = azuread_application.github_deploy.client_id
13	}
14	
15	resource "azuread_application_federated_identity_credential" "github_deploy" {
16	  application_id = azuread_application.github_deploy.id
17	  display_name   = "github-actions-${var.github_environment}"
18	  description    = "GitHub Actions OIDC for the ${var.github_environment} environment deploy"
19	  audiences      = ["api://AzureADTokenExchange"]
20	  issuer         = "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
21	  # Must match the workflow's `environment: production` job scoping.
22	  subject = "repo:${var.github_repo}:environment:${var.github_environment}"
23	}
24	
25	# Least privilege: scope Contributor to ONLY the three deploy targets, not the
26	# whole RG — dataq-rg is SHARED with the harness, so an RG-wide grant would let
27	# the CI principal modify harness resources too. The workflow only runs
28	# `az containerapp update` (api/worker) + `job start` (migrate); the SWA upload
29	# uses a separate static-web-apps API token, not this principal.
30	locals {
31	  github_deploy_targets = {
32	    api     = azurerm_container_app.api.id
33	    worker  = azurerm_container_app.worker.id

```
1	# DataQ — app infra (Terraform)
2	
3	Provisions the DataQ **application's own** production resources into the existing
4	`dataq-rg`. Separate from the harness stack
5	(`~/Coding/Python/DataQ-harness/terraform`, ADR 0021), **except** for three shared
6	resources forced by free/trial subscription caps (1 Container App Environment and
7	1 Postgres Flexible Server per subscription — see ADR 0024):
8	
9	- the **subscription** + **resource group** (`dataq-rg`),
10	- the **Container Apps environment** `dataq-cae` (neutral name, `purpose=dataq-shared`),
11	- the **Postgres Flexible Server** `dataq-pg-wus3-*` (neutral, `purpose=dataq-shared`).
12	
13	Both shared resources are **owned by the harness Terraform**; this stack only
14	*references* them (data sources). Everything the app creates is `dataq-app-*` /
15	`purpose=dataq-app`; the harness's `dataq-harness-*` resources are untouched.
16	
17	## What it creates
18	
19	| Resource | Name |
20	|---|---|
21	| Log Analytics workspace | `dataq-app-logs` |
22	| Application Insights | `dataq-app-ai` |
23	| User-assigned identity | `dataq-app-id` (api/worker → Key Vault) |
24	| Key Vault (RBAC) | `dataq-app-kv-<suffix>` (SecretStore + webhook secrets) |
25	| API / worker / migrate | `dataq-app-api` · `dataq-app-worker` · `dataq-app-migrate` (job) |
26	| Redis broker (Container App) | `dataq-app-redis` (internal TCP, password-auth) |
27	| Static Web App (Standard) | `dataq-app-web` (+ linked `dataq-app-api` backend) |
28	| Azure AD SSO app regs | `dataq-app-api-sso` (API) + `dataq-app-spa` (SPA) |
29	| GitHub-deploy app registration | `dataq-github-deploy` (OIDC federated cred) |
30	
31	**Referenced, not created:** the `dataq-cae` environment and the
32	`dataq-pg-wus3-*` server (both harness-owned). The app's database is a **distinct
33	`dataq` database** + least-privilege **`dataq_app`** role on the shared server.
34	
35	Backend image: `ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-backend:<image_tag>` (GHCR, public —
36	ACA pulls anonymously, ADR 0023). Must exist + be **public** before apply.
37	
38	## Prerequisites
39	
40	- `az login` as a subscription **Owner** (registers RPs; creates role assignments,
41	  AAD app registrations, and Key Vault secrets). **Do not** `source` the harness
42	  `secrets.sh` — that switches Terraform to the harness SP, which lacks Key Vault
43	  data-plane rights (403) and isn't the right identity for this stack.
44	- The shared `dataq-cae` env + `dataq-pg-wus3-*` server already exist (harness).
45	- The GHCR backend image pushed + public.
46	- The `dataq` database + `dataq_app` role provisioned (one-off, below).
47	- State is **local + gitignored**.
48	
49	## Shared Postgres — one-off role + database
50	
51	The app's DB lives on the shared server but is provisioned **out-of-band** (keeps
52	this stack connection-free / CI-friendly — no postgres provider). Run once,
53	connected as the server admin (add a temp firewall rule for your IP first):
54	
55	```sql
56	-- as the server admin, against the `postgres` database:
57	CREATE ROLE dataq_app LOGIN PASSWORD '<generated>';
58	CREATE DATABASE dataq OWNER dataq_app;
59	-- then, connected to the `dataq` database (PG15+ doesn't grant the db owner
60	-- CREATE on public by default):
61	GRANT ALL ON SCHEMA public TO dataq_app;
62	ALTER SCHEMA public OWNER TO dataq_app;
63	```
64	
65	Pass that password at apply time as `TF_VAR_app_db_password` (it becomes the
66	`DATABASE_URL` Container App secret; never committed). The app reaches the server
67	at runtime over the server's allow-Azure-services firewall rule.
68	
69	## Apply
70	
71	```bash
72	cd deploy/terraform
73	terraform init
74	TF_VAR_app_db_password='REDACTED' terraform plan    # review
75	TF_VAR_app_db_password='REDACTED' terraform apply
76	```
77	
78	## After apply — wire the Deploy workflow
79	
80	`.github/workflows/deploy.yml` reads these. Push them with `gh` from the outputs:
81	
82	```bash
83	gh secret  set AZURE_CLIENT_ID       -b "$(terraform output -raw github_actions_client_id)"
84	gh secret  set AZURE_TENANT_ID       -b "$(terraform output -raw azure_tenant_id)"
85	gh secret  set AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID -b "$(terraform output -raw azure_subscription_id)"
86	gh secret  set AZURE_STATIC_WEB_APPS_API_TOKEN -b "$(terraform output -raw swa_api_token)"
87	gh variable set AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP -b "$(terraform output -raw resource_group)"
88	gh variable set API_APP_NAME         -b "$(terraform output -raw api_app_name)"
89	gh variable set WORKER_APP_NAME      -b "$(terraform output -raw worker_app_name)"
90	gh variable set MIGRATE_JOB_NAME     -b "$(terraform output -raw migrate_job_name)"
91	gh variable set VITE_AZURE_TENANT_ID    -b "$(terraform output -raw azure_tenant_id)"
92	gh variable set VITE_AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID -b "$(terraform output -raw azure_spa_client_id)"
93	gh variable set VITE_AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID -b "$(terraform output -raw azure_api_client_id)"
94	gh variable set VITE_AZURE_API_SCOPE    -b "$(terraform output -raw azure_api_scope)"
95	```
96	
97	Create the `production` GitHub environment (federated-credential subject
98	`repo:<owner>/<repo>:environment:production`). **One-time GHCR step:** in the
99	`dataq-backend` package settings, *Connect repository* + grant the repo Actions
100	**write** access so the workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN` can push (label-linking alone
101	doesn't grant it for user-scoped packages).
102	
103	## Verify
104	
105	```bash
106	# App resources only — harness untouched:
107	az resource list -g dataq-rg --query "[?tags.purpose=='dataq-app'].name" -o tsv
108	
109	# API up (401 = healthy + auth-enforced):
110	curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" "$(terraform output -raw api_url)/api/v1/runs"
111	
112	# SPA + same-origin /api proxy:
113	curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" "$(terraform output -raw swa_url)/"
114	```
115	
```

The ADR §5 frames this as a "clean rebuild." What I actually implemented is a **targeted `terraform apply`** (destroys only the SWA; api/worker update in place; adds the frontend app) — safer than a full teardown. Let me record the as-built mechanism concisely:

  "old_string": "5. **Deployed-app cutover (amends ADR 0024).** Runtime `/config.js` is served by the nginx\n   **container**, but prod serves the UI from **Static Web App** (static, no runtime\n   injection). So the frontend moves **SWA → a Container App**. Adopt via a **clean\n   rebuild**: remove the DataQ app (api + worker + migrate job + SWA) and rebuild from the\n   new images, **keeping Key Vault, App Insights / Log Analytics, the shared Postgres +\n   `dataq` DB, and Redis as-is**. The deployed app runs `DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=oidc` against the\n   real tenant. AWS/GCP deploy IaC is **post-v1** (#505).",
  "new_string": "5. **Deployed-app cutover (amends ADR 0024).** Runtime `/config.js` is served by the nginx\n   **container**, but prod serves the UI from **Static Web App** (static, no runtime\n   injection). So the frontend moves **SWA → a Container App** (`dataq-app-frontend`),\n   **keeping Key Vault, App Insights / Log Analytics, the shared Postgres + `dataq` DB, and\n   Redis as-is**. The deployed app runs `DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=oidc` against the real tenant.\n   AWS/GCP deploy IaC is **post-v1** (#505).\n\n   **As implemented (Terraform):** a *targeted* apply, not a literal teardown — Terraform\n   destroys only the SWA (`azurerm_static_web_app` + its `null_resource` linked-backend) and\n   creates the frontend Container App; **api + worker update in place** (only `PUBLIC_BASE_URL`\n   changes) and the migrate job is untouched. Two mechanisms make this clean:\n   - **Deterministic FQDNs break the api↔frontend cycle.** The frontend needs the api URL as\n     its `/api` proxy upstream and the api needs the frontend URL (`PUBLIC_BASE_URL` + the SPA\n     redirect), which as resource references would be a Terraform cycle. Both URLs are instead\n     computed as `https://<app-name>.<env-default-domain>` from the shared environment data\n     source, so neither resource references the other.\n   - **Cloud-neutral nginx resolver.** The `/api` upstream is resolved at request time through\n     a variable, which needs a `resolver`; the image detects it from `/etc/resolv.conf` at\n     startup (nginx's `NGINX_ENTRYPOINT_LOCAL_RESOLVERS`) instead of a baked-in `127.0.0.11`,\n     so the one image works in compose (embedded DNS) and ACA/K8s (cluster DNS). nginx forwards\n     the upstream host as `Host` (+ TLS SNI) so ACA's Envoy routes `/api` to the api app."
}

+++ b/deploy/terraform/frontend.tf
@@ -0,0 +1,72 @@
+# DataQ frontend on Container Apps (ADR 0028 §5 cutover — replaces the Static Web
+# App, swa.tf). ONE generic nginx image (ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-frontend),
+# pulled anonymously (public GHCR package, ADR 0023). Nothing is baked in: the SPA
+# auth config + the /api proxy upstream are injected at RUNTIME via the DATAQ_*
+# env below (nginx envsubst → /config.js + the proxy_pass upstream). This is why
+# SWA couldn't host it — a static host can't inject runtime config.
+#
+# External ingress on 8080. The nginx conf reverse-proxies /api + /mcp to the api
+# Container App (same-origin, no CORS — the api keeps CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS empty),
+# so this app is the single public product surface; the api stays externally
+# reachable too (Azure Monitor→ADF webhook posts to PUBLIC_BASE_URL/api/...).
+
+resource "azurerm_container_app" "frontend" {
+  name                         = "dataq-app-frontend"
+  container_app_environment_id = data.azurerm_container_app_environment.shared.id
+  resource_group_name          = data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name
+  revision_mode                = "Single"
+
+  ingress {
+    external_enabled = true
+    target_port      = 8080
+    transport        = "auto"
+    traffic_weight {
+      latest_revision = true
+      percentage      = 100
+    }
+  }
+
+  template {
+    min_replicas = 1
+    max_replicas = 2
+    container {
+      name   = "frontend"
+      image  = "${var.frontend_image_repo}:${var.frontend_image_tag}"
+      cpu    = 0.25
+      memory = "0.5Gi"
+
+      # Proxy upstream — the api Container App's public FQDN (computed from the env
+      # domain to avoid a resource cycle; see local.api_public_url). nginx sends
+      # the matching Host + TLS SNI so ACA's Envoy routes it to the api.
+      env {
+        name  = "DATAQ_API_UPSTREAM"
+        value = local.api_public_url
+      }
+
+      # Runtime auth config (generic DATAQ_AUTH_* contract, ADR 0028). Real OIDC
+      # against Azure AD: mode=oidc + the SPA client + the tenant v2 authority +
+      # the full API scope. Validated end-to-end against this exact tenant in the
+      # #504 stage-3 pass. `mode=oidc` (anything != "bypass") keeps bypass OFF.
+      env {
+        name  = "DATAQ_AUTH_MODE"
+        value = "oidc"
+      }
+      env {
+        name  = "DATAQ_AUTH_AUTHORITY"
+        value = "https://login.microsoftonline.com/${local.azure_tenant_id}/v2.0"
+      }
+      env {
+        name  = "DATAQ_AUTH_CLIENT_ID"
+        value = azuread_application.spa.client_id
+      }
+      # Full scope string the SPA requests for the API access token
+      # (api://<api-client-id>/<scope>), per the config.ts apiScope contract.
+      env {
+        name  = "DATAQ_AUTH_API_SCOPE"
+        value = "api://${azuread_application.api.client_id}/${var.azure_api_scope}"
+      }
+    }
+  }
+
+  tags = local.common_tags
+}

20	
21	### 1. What you must change (never ship the eval/dev defaults)
22	
23	The prebuilt-image quickstart ([docs/getting-started](../docs/getting-started.md)) is a
24	**dev-bypass eval stack** — it disables auth, uses a passwordless DB, and binds to
25	loopback. A production deployment must flip all of the following. Values live in
26	[`deploy/.env.app.prod.example`](.env.app.prod.example) (app settings) +
27	[`deploy/terraform/variables.tf`](terraform/variables.tf) (infra):
28	
29	| Setting | Eval default | Production |
30	|---|---|---|
31	| `AUTH_DEV_BYPASS` | `true` | **`false`** — this is the master auth switch; leaving it on means **no authentication at all**. |
32	| `AZURE_TENANT_ID` / `AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID` / `AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID` | empty | your Azure AD tenant + the two app registrations (API + SPA). |
33	| **Frontend build** | prebuilt `:dev` image (bypass baked in) | **rebuild the SPA from source with your `VITE_AZURE_*`** — Vite bakes auth config at build time, so no prebuilt image can carry your tenant (the published `:latest` has none baked and shows the "not configured" banner). See [frontend/Dockerfile](../frontend/Dockerfile). |
34	| `SECRET_STORE` | `redis` (eval) | **`azure_key_vault`** + `AZURE_KEY_VAULT_URL` + the managed identity's `AZURE_CLIENT_ID` (#408). |
35	| `DATABASE_URL` / `REDIS_URL` | inline, passwordless | Key Vault-backed Container Apps secrets — **never literals**; real credentials. |
36	| `CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS` | n/a (same-origin) | empty **if** the SWA links the API same-origin; else the SPA origin. |
37	| `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` | n/a | the public origin (used to assemble webhook URLs). |
38	| `WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS` | seeded dev user | a **minimal** real allowlist — admins can read every suite's failing-row samples (see [Operational notes](#operational-notes)). |
39	| `APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING` | unset | your App Insights resource (observability). |
40	| `key_vault_purge_protection` (Terraform) | `false` (bring-up) | **`true`** for a hardened vault (irreversible). |
41	| Interactive API docs | served | **404 in prod** via the prod-docs gate (`ENVIRONMENT=prod`). |
42	
43	### 2. Access you need
44	
45	- **Azure subscription** — rights to create the resource group, Container Apps
46	  environment, PostgreSQL Flexible Server, Cache for Redis, Key Vault, Application
47	  Insights + Log Analytics, and the Static Web App (Contributor on the RG/subscription),
48	  **plus** `User Access Administrator`/`Owner` to grant the managed identity the **Key
49	  Vault Secrets User** role (an RBAC role assignment).
```

73	#### Azure — supported today
74	
75	- An Azure **subscription** + a region with quota for **1 Container Apps environment**,
76	  **1 PostgreSQL Flexible Server**, Cache for Redis, Key Vault, App Insights + Log
77	  Analytics, and a Static Web App. (Free/trial tiers cap one ACA env + one Postgres
78	  server per subscription, so the app **shares** the RG/env/Postgres server with the
79	  harness and namespaces its own DB + role — ADR [0024](../docs/adr/0024-app-deployment-infrastructure.md).)
80	- The **resource providers** and **app registrations** from §2 registered/created.
81	- The **GHCR** backend package public. Then follow [One-time provisioning](#one-time-provisioning).
82	
83	#### AWS — planned (not yet available)
84	
85	Not yet implemented. The seams map to: ECS Fargate or App Runner (api + worker) · RDS
86	for PostgreSQL · ElastiCache for Redis · Secrets Manager (`SecretStore` impl) · CloudWatch
87	+ OpenTelemetry (observability) · Cognito or an OIDC IdP behind `get_current_user`. Track
88	via the anti-lock-in roadmap ([ADR 0013](../docs/adr/0013-marketplace-distribution-and-anti-lock-in.md)).
89	
90	#### GCP — planned (not yet available)
91	
92	Not yet implemented. The seams map to: Cloud Run (api + worker) · Cloud SQL for
93	PostgreSQL · Memorystore for Redis · Secret Manager (`SecretStore` impl) · Cloud Logging +
94	OpenTelemetry · Identity Platform / an OIDC IdP behind `get_current_user`.
95	
96	## Topology
97	
98	```
99	Browser ─► Azure Static Web App (frontend/dist)
100	              │  /api/* proxied to the linked backend (same-origin → no CORS)
101	              ▼
102	        Azure Container Apps
103	          • dataq-api     (FastAPI image, external ingress :8000)
104	          • dataq-worker  (same image, `celery -A ... worker` + beat)
105	          • dataq-migrate (Container Apps Job: `alembic upgrade head`)
106	              │
107	              ├─► Azure Database for PostgreSQL (DATABASE_URL)
108	              ├─► Azure Cache for Redis        (REDIS_URL)
109	              ├─► Azure Key Vault              (SECRET_STORE=azure_key_vault, managed identity)
110	              └─► Application Insights         (APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING)
111	        GitHub Container Registry (GHCR) — holds the backend image (ADR 0023)
112	          ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-backend:<tag> — public package, so ACA
113	          pulls it anonymously (no registry credential stored on the apps/job).
114	```
115	
116	Both api + worker run the **same** image ([backend/Dockerfile](../backend/Dockerfile),
117	build context = repo root). The frontend is built and uploaded to SWA by the
118	workflow (the [frontend/Dockerfile](../frontend/Dockerfile) is the container
119	alternative — only needed if you run the UI on Container Apps instead of SWA).
120	
121	## One-time provisioning
122	
123	The datasource + compute infra is stood up by the external Terraform harness
124	(ADR 0021) — see `HARNESS_TODO.md`. Beyond that, this app needs:
125	
126	1. An **ACA environment** + the three apps/job above (the backend image is on
127	   **GHCR**, not ACR — ADR 0023). The api/worker run `uvicorn …` / `celery …`;
128	   the migrate **job** runs `alembic upgrade head`. The `deploy/terraform/` stack
129	   provisions all of this; the GHCR package must be **public** so ACA pulls it
130	   anonymously.
131	2. **Managed identity** on the api + worker apps with **Key Vault Secrets User**
132	   on the vault (so `DefaultAzureCredential` resolves `SECRET_STORE=azure_key_vault`).
133	3. **App env**: set the keys on the api + worker apps. The **complete** env-var
134	   reference (every Settings key) is [../.env.app.example](../.env.app.example);
135	   the prod-specific *values* are in [deploy/.env.app.prod.example](.env.app.prod.example).
136	   Secret values (DB/Redis URL, App Insights, webhook URLs) are Key Vault-backed
137	   Container Apps secrets — never literals. The user-assigned managed identity
138	   needs `AZURE_CLIENT_ID` set so `DefaultAzureCredential` resolves it (#408).
139	4. **SWA linked backend**: link the `dataq-api` Container App as the SWA backend so
140	   `/api/*` is proxied same-origin (then `CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS` can stay empty). If
141	   instead the SPA calls the API cross-origin, set `CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS` to the SWA
142	   origin (the FastAPI CORS middleware turns on only when it's non-empty).
143	5. **Azure Monitor → ADF webhook** alert rule (Week-7 task) — needs the deployed
144	   API URL; configure after the first deploy. Per [ADR 0006](../docs/adr/0006-adf-webhook-authentication.md)
145	   the shared secret rides the URL as a `?token=` query param, so don't
146	   hand-assemble it (wrong host / stale token after rotation / missing `?token=`
147	   are easy to get wrong — #92).
148	
149	   **Easiest path: the in-app webhook-config surface (#490).** Sign in as a
150	   workspace admin → **Settings → Webhooks** to copy the ready-to-paste ADF
151	   URL (host + current `?token=` from Key Vault) and the Airflow URL. Set
152	   `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` so the generated host is the public origin (the deploy sets
153	   it to the SWA host; empty falls back to the request host). Paste the ADF URL
154	   into the Action Group webhook field. Note the **live ADF delivery still needs
